items.body:
Codex is logged in with ChatGPT authentication and worked normally about an hour earlier, but now both Codex CLI and the ChatGPT desktop app fail on Codex requests while regular ChatGPT in the browser still works.

Reproduction:
- codex login status: Logged in using ChatGPT
- codex doctor reports stored API key: false
- codex doctor reports stored ChatGPT tokens: true
- codex doctor reports stored auth mode: chatgpt
- WebSocket handshake succeeds with HTTP 101
- Actual model stream repeatedly disconnects before response.completed
- Codex falls back from WebSockets to HTTPS
- HTTPS fallback returns 401 Unauthorized

This reproduces with:
- Codex 0.157.0 from Homebrew
- ChatGPT.app bundled Codex 0.155.0-alpha.9.2
- gpt-6-astra
- gpt-5.5

Environment:
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64
- No OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_*KEY environment variables
- auth.json has OPENAI_API_KEY set to null
- Logging out and back in with ChatGPT does not resolve it
- Browser ChatGPT continues to work

Example failed request IDs:
- 4eb6cb38-3273-4367-be4a-c8def67bdd52
- 5d110ca7-da30-4dd7-8bf7-11af544cbf94
- fc597bf4-e4db-42fb-b8cc-71c857fc3781

The sudden onset and reproduction across both CLI and ChatGPT Desktop make this look like a Codex-specific backend/session/auth transport issue rather than a local CLI configuration problem.

items.body:
### Summary

Codex CLI successfully authenticates using ChatGPT OAuth, and `codex doctor --json`
reports valid ChatGPT auth and successful WebSocket reachability.

However, actual inference requests fail.

The issue reproduces across:
- Windows 11
- macOS
- Linux VM

This makes a local OS/network configuration issue unlikely.

### Environment

Codex CLI:
- Version: 0.157.0
- Install method: npm
- Provider: openai
- Auth mode: ChatGPT OAuth

Windows environment:
- Windows 11 Professional
- Version: 10.0.26200
- Windows Terminal
- No OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable
- No CODEX_API_KEY environment variable
- No proxy environment variables

`codex login status`:

    Logged in using ChatGPT

`auth.json` contains:

    "OPENAI_API_KEY": null

and contains ChatGPT OAuth tokens.

`codex doctor --json` reports:

    "auth.credentials": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "auth is configured",
      "details": {
        "stored API key": "false",
        "stored ChatGPT tokens": "true",
        "stored auth mode": "chatgpt"
      }
    }

Configuration:

    "model provider": "openai"

Network reachability also succeeds:

    "ChatGPT inference URL": "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/<redacted> reachable (HTTP 405)"

WebSocket diagnostic succeeds:

    "Responses WebSocket handshake succeeded"

with:

    "auth mode": "chatgpt"
    "handshake result": "HTTP 101 Switching Protocols"
    "model provider": "openai"
    "wire API": "responses"

### Reproduction

1. Log out:

    codex logout

2. Perform a fresh OAuth/device login:

    codex login --device-auth

3. Login completes successfully:

    Successfully logged in

4. Verify:

    codex login status

Output:

    Logged in using ChatGPT

5. Run:

    codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Reply only with OK"

### Actual result

Codex starts normally:

    OpenAI Codex v0.157.0
    workdir: C:\Users\frost
    model: gpt-6-astra
    provider: openai
    approval: never
    sandbox: read-only
    reasoning effort: none

Then inference fails:

    ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
    ERROR: Reconnecting... 3/5
    ERROR: Reconnecting... 4/5
    ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
    warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport.
    stream disconnected before completion:
    websocket closed by server before response.completed
    ERROR: Reconnecting... 1/5

Earlier attempts also produced HTTP 401 responses referencing an API key
(`sk-svcac...`) even though:

- OPENAI_API_KEY was not present in the environment
- CODEX_API_KEY was not present in the environment
- auth.json had `"OPENAI_API_KEY": null`
- `codex doctor` reported `stored API key: false`
- authentication mode was `chatgpt`

### Cross-platform reproduction

The same underlying failure reproduces using the same ChatGPT account on:

- Windows
- macOS
- Linux VM

Fresh login does not resolve it.

### Expected behavior

After a successful ChatGPT OAuth login, Codex should use the stored ChatGPT
credentials and complete inference requests normally.

If WebSocket transport fails, HTTPS fallback should successfully complete the
request instead of entering another reconnect loop.

Codex should never attempt to use or report an unrelated/stale API key while
the active authentication mode is ChatGPT and no API-key credentials are
configured.

### Diagnostics already performed

- Fresh `codex login --device-auth`
- Confirmed `codex login status`
- Checked OPENAI_API_KEY: absent
- Checked CODEX_API_KEY: absent
- Checked User and Machine environment variables: absent
- Checked auth.json: API key is null
- `codex doctor --json`: auth OK
- Provider reachability: OK
- WebSocket handshake diagnostic: HTTP 101
- Reproduced on three operating systems
- Reproduced outside a Git repo with `--skip-git-repo-check`

### Additional diagnostic details

The Windows `codex doctor --json` output showed:
- Codex version: 0.157.0
- Auth storage mode: File
- Stored API key: false
- Stored ChatGPT tokens: true
- Stored auth mode: chatgpt
- Model provider: openai
- No proxy environment variables
- Responses WebSocket handshake: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols
- Wire API: responses

This suggests local credential parsing and endpoint reachability are healthy, while the real inference stream fails after connection establishment.

items.title: [Windows] Codex Desktop/CLI returns 401 sk-svcac despite valid ChatGPT OAuth token; direct bearer request is accepted

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop and Codex CLI both fail with:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

The user is authenticated with a ChatGPT Pro account, not an API key.

The important finding is that the OAuth access token stored in `~/.codex/auth.json` is accepted by the same backend when used directly as a Bearer token. The direct request returns HTTP 400 only because no model is supplied, proving that the OAuth token itself is valid.

This appears consistent with the wave of similar reports on 2026-09-25, including #48262, #48264, #48267, #48270, etc.

## Environment

- Platform: Windows
- ChatGPT subscription: Pro
- Codex CLI: `0.156.1`
- Auth mode: ChatGPT
- Endpoint failing: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

## Initial error

From ChatGPT Desktop:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
cf-ray: a40da1b6fbb8a648-GRU
request id: 565e50e9-4a45-43a3-81e0-4234809b22fe
```

## Checks performed

### 1. Environment variables

Checked for:

- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `CODEX_API_KEY`
- `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `OPENAI_BASE_URL`

None were present.

### 2. ChatGPT logout/login

Completely logged out of ChatGPT Desktop, closed the app, reopened it and logged back in.

No change.

### 3. `~/.codex/auth.json`

Inspected without printing secrets:

```
AuthFileExists  : True
AuthMode        : chatgpt
HasApiKey       : False
HasTokens       : True
HasRefreshToken : True
LastRefresh     : 2026-09-25T22:58:11.762532700Z
```

So:

- auth mode is `chatgpt`
- no `OPENAI_API_KEY` is stored
- access/refresh tokens exist
- token refresh was recent

### 4. `~/.codex/config.toml`

Searched for:

- `model_provider`
- `base_url`
- `chatgpt_base_url`
- `env_key`
- `preferred_auth_method`
- `forced_login_method`

No matches.

### 5. CLI authentication status

```
PS> codex --version
codex-cli 0.156.1

PS> codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

### 6. CLI reproduction

Command:

```
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only "Reply only with OK."
```

Result:

```
model: gpt-6-sol
provider: openai
...
ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 3/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 4/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport. stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
ERROR: Reconnecting... 1/5
...
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
ERROR: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
cf-ray: a40dad3d596e58f7-GRU
request id: 2549c946-bb14-4eb6-9b81-f2da468d8434
```

### 7. Fresh Device Code login

Backed up `auth.json`, then:

```
codex logout
codex login --device-auth
```

Device authorization completed successfully with the same ChatGPT account.

After re-authenticating, the CLI still failed with the same masked service credential suffix:

```
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
cf-ray: a40db51e7eb3f1d5-GRU
request id: 82c29d97-aed2-4fd0-b99a-62947f6de0ab
```

### 8. Direct bearer-token test against the same backend

Loaded `tokens.access_token` from `~/.codex/auth.json` and sent it directly as:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {}
```

Result:

```
HTTP 400

{
  "detail": "The 'None' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."
}
```

This is the key finding: the backend accepts the OAuth token and recognizes it as a ChatGPT-account Codex request. It is not returning 401 for the stored OAuth token.

### 9. `codex login --with-access-token`

The same known-valid OAuth access token was then piped to:

```
codex login --with-access-token
```

After that, running:

```
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only "Reply only with OK."
```

still produced the same failure:

```
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport
...
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
cf-ray: a40dbe603a607e26-GRU
request id: cfa49edc-d932-422e-82eb-7c43c493c17e
```

## Expected behavior

When authenticated via ChatGPT OAuth, Codex CLI/Desktop should use the valid ChatGPT OAuth credentials and successfully send the request to the Codex backend.

## Actual behavior

The valid OAuth token is accepted when used directly, but Codex CLI/Desktop requests fail with a different credential identified by the backend as an invalid `sk-svcac...` key.

The same masked suffix `...fvMA` persists after:

- logout/login
- fresh device-code authentication
- recent token refresh
- absence of API-key environment variables
- absence of custom provider/base URL configuration
- explicit `--with-access-token` login

## Additional observation

The CLI first fails over WebSockets, retries, then falls back to HTTPS. The final HTTPS request also returns the same 401, so this does not appear to be only a WebSocket transport problem.

No secret/token values are included in this report.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex Desktop 26.924.20706

Also reproduced with downgraded Codex Desktop builds.

CLI binaries tested:
- npm/NVM Codex CLI 0.144.1
- standalone Codex CLI 0.157.0
- Codex Desktop bundled CLI 0.158.0-alpha.2

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64

PowerShell 7.6.6

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex authentication succeeds locally, but both Codex Desktop and Codex CLI fail with HTTP 401 when sending requests to the Codex backend.

ChatGPT itself (web/app) works normally.

`codex login status` reports:

```
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

However, sending a trivial prompt such as `test` returns:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac***fvMA.
You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys.,
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

The same masked `sk-svcac…fvMA` credential is reported repeatedly.

This is similar to #41975, but this report is on Windows and the backend explicitly reports `Incorrect API key provided`.

### Troubleshooting already performed

1. Confirmed `codex login status` says `Logged in using ChatGPT`.
2. Ran `codex logout`.
3. Confirmed `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json` was removed after logout.
4. Performed a fresh ChatGPT login using the standalone Codex binary.
5. Re-tested after the fresh login; the same 401 error returned.
6. Tested multiple Codex CLI versions:
   - 0.144.1
   - 0.157.0
   - Desktop bundled 0.158.0-alpha.2
7. Tested Codex Desktop current and downgraded versions; the same 401 persists.
8. Confirmed there are no `OPENAI*` or `CODEX*` environment variables set in the PowerShell session.
9. Confirmed `CODEX_HOME` is not overridden.
10. Checked `~/.codex/config.toml`: no custom `base_url`, `model_provider`, or OpenAI API key override is configured.
11. ChatGPT itself continues to work normally with the same account.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to Codex using ChatGPT.
2. Run:
   ```
   codex login status
   ```
3. Observe:
   ```
   Logged in using ChatGPT
   ```
4. Start Codex Desktop or CLI.
5. Send a simple prompt such as:
   ```
   test
   ```
6. Observe HTTP 401 from:
   ```
   https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
   ```
   with:
   ```
   Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac***fvMA
   ```

### Expected behavior

After successfully signing in with ChatGPT, Codex Desktop/CLI should use the valid ChatGPT/Codex credentials and send requests normally.

### Additional information

Model when reproducing:
```
GPT-6-Astra low
```

Example recent request IDs:
- `ab70b99e-5fa3-49df-bdbc-b553eb737913`
- `5103c947-d3f8-45d4-b63b-c53373748095`
- `c5d19b9f-cfef-4fac-92c5-429fb64b0e1e`
- `33be28c2-943c-4f23-a4b6-70bb5f149fdf`

Cloudflare rays observed across reproductions included both WAW and BUD PoPs, while the error remained identical.

Because the issue reproduces across multiple Codex versions and after a complete local logout/fresh ChatGPT login, this appears to be related to the ChatGPT-to-Codex credential/account state rather than a single local Codex build.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex CLI cannot complete any model request when authenticated using ChatGPT.

`codex login status` reports:

Logged in using ChatGPT

`codex doctor --json` reports that authentication is correctly configured with:
- stored API key: false
- stored ChatGPT tokens: true
- stored auth mode: chatgpt

HTTP provider reachability succeeds and the Responses WebSocket handshake succeeds with HTTP 101.

However, sending even a simple prompt such as `hello` fails with:

stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed

unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...[REDACTED]...fvMA.
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

Recent request ID:
47f75140-dd8c-46b4-93f0-037c6ce0b49d

The same problem also occurs when using Codex through the ChatGPT app connected to this remote SSH workspace.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install/run Codex CLI 0.157.0 on a remote Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 host.
2. Authenticate using ChatGPT:
   codex logout
   codex login --device-auth
3. Verify:
   codex login status
   -> Logged in using ChatGPT
4. Verify that no OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_* API credential is present in the shell environment.
5. Start Codex:
   codex
6. Send a simple prompt such as:
   hello
7. The request fails with HTTP 401 and reports an incorrect `sk-svcac...` API key.

I also found that the background app-server was initially 0.153.4 while the CLI was 0.157.0. I stopped the old app-server processes and allowed Codex to reinstall/restart it. `codex doctor --json` now confirms both CLI and app-server are 0.157.0, but the 401 still occurs.

I also performed an A/B authentication test directly against:

https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

using the ChatGPT `access_token` already stored in ~/.codex/auth.json, without printing or exposing the token.

With the stored ChatGPT access token:
HTTP 400
{"detail":"The 'None' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}

Without Authorization:
HTTP 401
{"detail":"Unauthorized"}

This suggests the stored ChatGPT access token is accepted by the backend, while the actual Codex request is being authenticated differently or incorrectly.

I did NOT include or expose any access_token, refresh_token, id_token, or auth.json contents.

### What is the expected behavior?

When `codex login status` reports `Logged in using ChatGPT` and valid ChatGPT tokens are stored, Codex should authenticate requests to the ChatGPT Codex backend using those credentials and successfully process prompts.

Codex should not send or resolve to an invalid `sk-svcac...` credential when no API key is configured or stored.

### Additional information

Troubleshooting already performed:

- Updated Codex CLI to 0.157.0.
- `codex logout` followed by `codex login --device-auth`.
- Confirmed `codex login status` = Logged in using ChatGPT.
- Confirmed no OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_* API credential in the shell environment.
- Confirmed config.toml has model provider `openai` and no custom model_provider/base_url.
- Confirmed `codex doctor` reports stored API key = false and stored ChatGPT tokens = true.
- Confirmed HTTP reachability to the ChatGPT inference endpoint.
- Confirmed Responses WebSocket handshake succeeds (HTTP 101).
- Restarted/reinstalled the stale app-server so both CLI and app-server are now 0.157.0.
- The issue reproduces in both CLI and the ChatGPT/Codex remote SSH workflow.
- A direct request using the stored ChatGPT access token passes authentication and reaches model validation (HTTP 400 for missing model), while the same request without authentication returns HTTP 401.

This appears similar to #41975.

Please let me know if additional redacted logs or diagnostics would help. I can provide them without exposing authentication tokens.

items.body:
### What version of Codex are you using?

- Codex CLI: 0.157.0
- Codex Desktop: 26.924.1866.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT paid plan

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11, x86_64
OS build reported by `codex doctor --json`: `10.0.26200`

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop and Codex CLI both fail every prompt with:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac********...fvMA.
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

The key ending in `fvMA` was created around April and had not been intentionally used afterward. I revoked it after this problem appeared, but Codex continues trying to use the exact same credential in both Desktop and CLI.

This is unexpected because Codex is authenticated with ChatGPT, not API-key auth.

`codex login status` reports:

```
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

`codex doctor --json` reports:

```
auth credentials: ok
auth file: C:\Users\qwesz\.codex\auth.json
auth storage mode: File
stored API key: false
stored ChatGPT tokens: true
stored auth mode: chatgpt
model provider: openai
```

Network diagnostics also pass:
- ChatGPT inference endpoint reachable
- Responses WebSocket handshake succeeds with HTTP 101
- No proxy environment variables are configured

### When did it start?

The issue started immediately after I archived several Codex conversations. Before that, Codex was working normally.

Interestingly, `codex doctor --json` also reports thread/archive state inconsistencies:

```
rollout files and state DB thread inventory differ
4 active rollout files missing matching DB rows
22 archived rollout files missing matching DB rows
18 duplicate rollout thread IDs
```

I do not know whether this is related to the authentication failure, but the timing matches the conversation-archiving action.

### Troubleshooting already performed

I have already tried all of the following:

1. Confirmed these environment variables are unset:
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `CODEX_API_KEY`
   - `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`
2. Confirmed `auth.json` uses `auth_mode = chatgpt`.
3. Confirmed `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not present in `auth.json`.
4. Rebuilt `auth.json` from a fresh ChatGPT login.
5. Checked `config.toml`; no API-key/provider override was found.
6. Removed the Codex-related Windows Credential Manager entry.
7. Used Windows App Repair.
8. Used Windows App Reset.
9. Logged out of all ChatGPT sessions/devices and signed in again.
10. Tested a brand-new Desktop conversation.
11. Tested Codex CLI separately.
12. Confirmed Desktop and CLI both fail with the same `sk-svcac...fvMA` credential.
13. Confirmed `codex doctor --json` says installation/auth/network are otherwise healthy.

The revoked credential is therefore not coming from the current `auth.json`, environment variables, or the obvious Windows Credential Manager entry.

### Reproduction steps

1. Sign in to Codex using ChatGPT.
2. Verify:
   ```
   codex login status
   ```
   returns `Logged in using ChatGPT`.
3. Start Codex Desktop or Codex CLI.
4. Send a simple prompt such as `test`.
5. Request to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` fails with:
   ```
   401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
   ```
6. Re-login / reset auth.
7. The same revoked credential is still used.

### Expected behavior

When `auth_mode = chatgpt` and no API key is stored, Codex should use the active ChatGPT OAuth credentials and should not continue using a revoked `sk-svcac` credential.

### Additional diagnostics

Recent request ID from Desktop:

```
903797b0-e2dc-46c8-a3b0-dbb186d70e70
```

Another recent request ID:

```
44621b28-2bef-4951-9e38-0aeae90107ac
```

The full API key and ChatGPT tokens are intentionally omitted.

This looks similar to #41975, but this case is on Windows, Codex 0.157.0, and the backend error explicitly identifies the same revoked `sk-svcac` credential on every attempt.

Pro

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Windows Codex package:
OpenAI.Codex 26.903.8094.0

CLI versions tested:
0.153.4
0.148.0

Authentication:
codex login status -> Logged in using ChatGPT

Environment:
No OPENAI_*, CODEX_*, or CHATGPT_* environment variables

Config:
No API key/custom provider in ~/.codex/config.toml

Remediation already attempted:
- sign out/in
- Windows app reset
- rename/delete ~/.codex/auth.json
- fresh auth.json regenerated
- tested older CLI 0.148.0

Observed result:
Both CLI versions and Desktop return:

401 Unauthorized
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

Direct request using the freshly generated auth.json access_token:
- malformed request: 400 {"detail":"Input must be a list"}
- correctly shaped request: 401 invalid_api_key with the same sk-svcac... credential

Example request ID:
6da93189-86c6-424c-88d5-37edbee616d0

Example Cloudflare ray:
a40dc4334e38b78e-ORD

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install and launch the Windows Codex desktop app (`OpenAI.Codex 26.903.8094.0`).
2. Sign in using ChatGPT authentication.
3. Confirm that no `OPENAI_*`, `CODEX_*`, or `CHATGPT_*` environment variables are set.
4. Confirm that `~/.codex/config.toml` contains no API key or custom provider configuration.
5. Run the bundled CLI and verify authentication:

```powershell
& $codex --version
& $codex login status
```

Observed:

```text
codex-cli 0.153.4
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

6. Run a simple request:

```powershell
& $codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Reply with exactly: CODEX_AUTH_OK"
```

The client repeatedly reconnects, falls back from WebSockets to HTTPS, and then fails with:

```text
401 Unauthorized
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

Example failed session ID:

```text
01a0dadf-59a7-74e1-970b-8dce413a868d
```

Example request ID:

```text
6da93189-86c6-424c-88d5-37edbee616d0
```

Example CF-Ray:

```text
a40dc4334e38b78e-ORD
```

The same failure occurs in the Codex desktop app.

Troubleshooting already performed:

- Signed out and back into ChatGPT/Codex.
- Reset the Windows Codex app.
- Renamed `~/.codex/auth.json`; reopening Codex successfully generated a new `auth.json`.
- Verified `codex login status` still reports `Logged in using ChatGPT`.
- Verified there are no relevant API-key environment variables.
- Verified `config.toml` contains no API key.
- Tested an older standalone CLI (`codex-cli 0.148.0`) using the same ChatGPT login; it fails with the same `sk-svcac...` 401.
- Direct requests using the freshly generated `auth.json` token reach `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`, but a correctly structured request also results in the same `invalid_api_key` / `sk-svcac...` error.

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected behavior:

A ChatGPT-authenticated Codex session should use the ChatGPT authentication token and successfully send requests to the Codex backend.


Actual behavior:

Codex reports that it is logged in using ChatGPT, but requests are rejected as though an invalid `sk-svcac...` API key were being supplied.

Token-limit/context-window usage does not appear relevant; the failure occurs on a brand-new session with a trivial one-line prompt.

items.body:
## Summary

After a user-initiated Codex update, attempting to use Codex CLI on a PC resulted in approximately 20 separate terminal windows opening. The windows remained open rather than briefly flashing and disappearing. More windows continued to open while the user manually closed existing ones, making them difficult to dismiss. The user eventually stopped the application, after which the repeated spawning stopped; the precise shutdown method was not captured.

The user reports that things worked before the update. The timing suggests a possible regression, but the updated component and root cause have not been verified.

## What version of Codex CLI is running?

Not captured. Exact CLI/app versions before and after the update, and which component the update changed, are not confirmed.

## What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro, as reported by the user.

## Which model were you using?

Not captured.

## What platform is your computer?

PC. Exact operating system and build were not confirmed for this incident.

## What terminal emulator and version are you using?

Not captured. The executable names and contents of the spawned terminal windows are also unknown.

## Observed sequence

This is the user's reported sequence, not an independently tested reproducer:

1. Initiate a Codex update.
2. Attempt to use Codex CLI on the PC.
3. Observe approximately 20 separate terminal windows that remain open.
4. Close windows manually; new windows continue to appear while existing ones are being closed.
5. Stop the application to end the repeated window spawning.

## Expected behavior

Normal CLI use should not create a continuing stream of persistent terminal windows that the user cannot keep up with closing.

## Impact

Normal use was disrupted and the user had to stop the application.

## Diagnostics

No logs, screenshots, process tree, exact commands, or `codex doctor` output are available for this report. No root cause or relationship to an authentication failure is asserted.

## Possibly related reports

- #48152
- #48074
- #48059

These concern visible terminal/helper windows. The distinguishing observation here is that the windows **stayed open and accumulated**, with **new windows continuing to appear as the user closed them**, rather than only flashing briefly. A shared cause is not confirmed.

Submitted through ChatGPT at the affected user's explicit request, using only their description of the incident.

### What issue are you seeing?

## Title

[Windows][26.924.20706] ChatGPT-authenticated Codex fails with 401 and reports invalid sk-svcac API key

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT – Powered by Codex & OWL

**Version:** 26.924.20706
**Released:** September 25, 2026

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex in the ChatGPT Windows desktop application suddenly fails for every prompt.

It attempts to reconnect several times and then returns:

```text
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac********...fvMA.
You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys.
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
cf-ray: a40da65e3e6c69aa-LAX
request id: b2ae33d2-8be0-40fd-88d9-801d3657040a
```

This is unexpected because Codex is authenticated through my ChatGPT Pro account. I am not using an API key for Codex.

Regular ChatGPT continues to work normally in the same account.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT Desktop on Windows.
2. Open a Codex conversation/workspace.
3. Send any prompt.
4. Codex displays repeated `Reconnecting` attempts.
5. The request eventually fails with HTTP 401.
6. The backend error specifically reports an invalid `sk-svcac...` API key.

The problem occurs consistently.

### Authentication troubleshooting

I logged out of Codex and signed back in with ChatGPT.

Login succeeds, but the problem remains unchanged.

After signing back in:

`C:\Users\<user>\.codex\auth.json`

was freshly updated and reports:

```text
AuthMode       : chatgpt
ApiKeyStored   : False
TokensStored   : True
```

The auth file contains these fields:

```text
auth_mode, OPENAI_API_KEY, tokens, last_refresh
```

`OPENAI_API_KEY` is empty.

### Environment-variable troubleshooting

I checked the following Windows environment variables at Process, User, and Machine scope:

```text
OPENAI_API_KEY
CODEX_API_KEY
OPENAI_BASE_URL
```

All nine checks returned `False`.

There is therefore no OpenAI/Codex API key or base URL configured through the Windows environment.

### Codex configuration

`C:\Users\<user>\.codex\config.toml` contains only:

```toml
model = "gpt-6-astra"
```

There is no:

* custom model provider
* custom base URL
* API-key environment variable
* bearer-token override
* HTTP authorization/header configuration

### Expected behavior

With:

```text
auth_mode = chatgpt
```

Codex should authenticate to:

```text
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

using the ChatGPT authentication established by the desktop application.

### Actual behavior

Despite:

* successful ChatGPT login
* `auth_mode = chatgpt`
* valid ChatGPT tokens being present
* no API key stored in `auth.json`
* no API-key environment variables
* no custom provider/authentication configuration

the backend reports receiving/rejecting an API key beginning with:

```text
sk-svcac...
```

This credential does not appear to originate from the user's Codex configuration, Windows environment, or `auth.json`.

### Impact

Codex is currently unusable because all requests fail authentication.

Regular ChatGPT remains functional.

### Additional information

The API key reported in the error has been redacted. No credential values are included in this report.

Example failed request:

```text
Endpoint:
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

HTTP status:
401 Unauthorized

Request ID:
b2ae33d2-8be0-40fd-88d9-801d3657040a

Cloudflare Ray:
a40da65e3e6c69aa-LAX
```


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Open ChatGPT Desktop for Windows.
Open an existing Codex workspace/conversation.
Send a prompt, for example:
Let's do another run of the Filtered Pipeline.
Codex displays repeated Reconnecting attempts.
After several attempts, the request fails with HTTP 401.
The error reports an invalid API key beginning with sk-svcac..., despite Codex being authenticated using ChatGPT.

The issue reproduces consistently with different prompts.

Logging out of Codex and signing back in with ChatGPT does not resolve it.

The failure happens during the request/authentication stage, so token-limit or context-window usage does not appear relevant. I do not have a session ID exposed in the error UI.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should use the ChatGPT authentication associated with my signed-in ChatGPT Pro account and successfully send requests to:

https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

When auth_mode is chatgpt, no unrelated API-key credential should be used for the request.

### Additional information

Authentication state after signing out and back in:

auth_mode = chatgpt
OPENAI_API_KEY = empty
tokens = present

Windows environment-variable checks for the following variables at Process, User, and Machine scope all returned False:

OPENAI_API_KEY
CODEX_API_KEY
OPENAI_BASE_URL

The Codex config contains only:

model = "gpt-6-astra"

Regular ChatGPT works normally. Only Codex requests are failing.

Example failed request:

Endpoint:
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

HTTP status:
401 Unauthorized

Request ID:
b2ae33d2-8be0-40fd-88d9-801d3657040a

Cloudflare Ray:

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary

ChatGPT OAuth succeeds and the Codex backend accepts the OAuth bearer token directly, but Codex model requests for the GPT-5.6 family fail with:

```
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
```

This reproduces across multiple Codex CLI versions **and independently through OpenCode using ChatGPT Pro/Plus OAuth**, which strongly suggests a backend/model-routing credential issue rather than a local CLI auth/config issue.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- Auth mode: ChatGPT OAuth / ChatGPT Pro
- Provider: `openai`
- No `OPENAI_*`, `CODEX_*`, or `CHATGPT_*` environment variables
- No custom `model_provider` or `base_url`
- `codex doctor --json` reports:
  - stored API key: `false`
  - stored ChatGPT tokens: `true`
  - stored auth mode: `chatgpt`
  - model provider: `openai`
- `~/.codex/auth.json` contains OAuth tokens and `OPENAI_API_KEY: null`

## Versions reproduced

The same failure occurs on:

- `0.148.0`
- `0.156.0`
- `0.157.0`
- `0.159.0-alpha.3`

So this does not appear tied to a single npm release.

## Minimal Codex CLI repro

```bash
cd /tmp
codex exec \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  --ephemeral \
  -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  "Reply with exactly: AUTH_OK"
```

Observed:

```
ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
...
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport.
stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
...
ERROR: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

Fresh browser OAuth login and `codex login --device-auth` both reproduce the same failure.

## Direct OAuth bearer token is accepted

Using the `access_token` from the same `~/.codex/auth.json` directly against the Codex backend:

```
POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"gpt-5.6-sol"}
```

returns:

```
HTTP 400
{"detail":"Store must be set to false"}
```

This is important because it demonstrates that the freshly issued OAuth bearer token itself is accepted by the backend. The failure is not simply an invalid/expired ChatGPT login.

## Independent reproduction via OpenCode

I also authenticated OpenCode independently using the ChatGPT Pro/Plus OAuth flow.

A request for an unsupported model:

```
openai/gpt-5.2
```

returns the expected semantic error:

```
Bad Request: {"detail":"The 'gpt-5.2' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}
```

This shows the backend recognizes the request as a ChatGPT-authenticated Codex request.

But all tested GPT-5.6 models fail with the same masked service-account credential:

```
openai/gpt-5.6-luna  -> Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
openai/gpt-5.6-sol   -> Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
openai/gpt-5.6-terra -> Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
```

The masked key suffix is the same as the one returned through the official Codex CLI.

## Why this looks server-side

Two independent clients using ChatGPT OAuth reproduce the same `sk-svcacct` credential failure, while direct use of the actual OAuth bearer token reaches the same backend successfully and gets a normal request-validation response.

The failure therefore appears to occur downstream of ChatGPT OAuth authentication, potentially during Codex model routing / inference dispatch, where an internal service credential is being rejected.

## Impact

This fully blocks Codex usage on a paid ChatGPT Pro account, including existing development workflows, despite successful authentication and available subscription quota.

Please let me know if additional request IDs, timestamps, or diagnostics would help.

items.title: Prevent Windows daemon launches from retaining launcher stdio
items.body:
Prevent Windows daemon launches from retaining launcher stdio

## Why

Detached Windows daemons can inherit the launcher's output pipes, leaving callers waiting for EOF after the launcher exits.

## What changed

Clear inheritance flags on the launcher's standard handles before spawning managed Windows processes. Leave the flags cleared to protect concurrent launches while preserving the child's configured stdio, and tolerate missing or already-closed handles.

## Testing

- Add a Windows regression test verifying that captured launcher output closes while the detached child remains alive and writes to its configured log.
- Give optional MCP startup grace tests more time to complete on slow runners while keeping the pending server's startup timeout longer than the turn timeout.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Codex App on Windows is consistently failing after my 5-hour usage window reset. New conversations and very simple prompts fail with either:

```
stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
```

followed by / alternating with:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac-[REDACTED]
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

I am signed in with ChatGPT Plus, not an API key.

### Timeline / possible trigger

1. I was working on a project using GPT-6 Luna Max with acceleration. It was very slow and repeatedly errored.
2. I temporarily switched to Astra 6 Max with acceleration.
3. Astra answered only one question and, in under one minute, consumed about 56% of my 5-hour allowance. I stopped it immediately because only ~1% remained.
4. I switched back to GPT-6 Luna Max with acceleration and did not use Astra again.
5. I waited for the next 5-hour reset.
6. As soon as the 5-hour window reset, Codex began consistently failing with WebSocket disconnects and 401 errors.
7. The problem continues in brand-new conversations and also reproduces at Medium reasoning effort.

I am not claiming the Astra usage caused the authentication failure, but the timing may be relevant.

### Authentication diagnostics

Local auth state:

```
auth_mode = chatgpt
OPENAI_API_KEY exists = False
```

`auth.json` contains the expected ChatGPT OAuth fields:

```
id_token
access_token
refresh_token
account_id
```

No OPENAI or CODEX environment variables are present.

No `api_key`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `model_provider`, `base_url`, `chatgpt`, or `responses` overrides are present in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

Relevant Codex log diagnostics (secrets redacted):

```
auth_header_attached=true
auth_header_name="authorization"
auth_mode="Chatgpt"
auth_retry_after_unauthorized="true"
auth_recovery_mode="managed"
auth_recovery_phase="refresh_token"

auth_env_openai_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_enabled=false

auth_recovery_followup_success="false"
auth_recovery_followup_status="401"
```

The server response simultaneously recognizes my ChatGPT plan and usage state:

```
x-codex-active-limit: premium
x-codex-plan-type: plus
x-codex-primary-used-percent: 0
x-codex-secondary-used-percent: 39
x-codex-primary-window-minutes: 300
x-codex-secondary-window-minutes: 10080
```

So the backend appears to recognize the Plus account and that the 5-hour window has reset, while the request still fails as an incorrect API key. Token refresh is attempted and the follow-up request still returns 401.

### Request IDs / Cloudflare rays

Failure 1:

```
request id: d9198167-3556-4d49-a534-579707df43ae
cf-ray: a40dc149bb38f244-KHH
```

Failure 2 (new conversation / another test):

```
request id: 48b2d4b5-923a-4321-9f93-52ed137bad64
cf-ray: a40dc4e39ffbf1f4-KHH
```

### Troubleshooting already performed

- Signed out and signed back into Codex App with ChatGPT.
- Confirmed `auth_mode = chatgpt`.
- Confirmed `OPENAI_API_KEY` in auth.json is empty.
- Confirmed no OPENAI/CODEX environment variables.
- Confirmed no custom model provider/base URL/API-key settings in config.toml.
- Tested a brand-new conversation with a trivial prompt.
- Tested a different reasoning effort.
- Codex's managed refresh-token recovery runs, but the follow-up still returns 401.

I have intentionally not deleted the entire `.codex` directory because the logs indicate ChatGPT OAuth is selected correctly and the backend recognizes the Plus entitlement.

### Expected behavior

After the 5-hour usage window resets, Codex App should continue using my ChatGPT OAuth credentials and Plus entitlement normally. It should not route or reinterpret the authenticated request as an invalid `sk-svcac...` API key.

### Additional note

The unexpectedly large usage event immediately before this began may also be worth checking: Astra 6 Max with acceleration consumed approximately 56% of the 5-hour allowance in under one minute for a single question.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex CLI: 0.157.0 Codex Desktop: [Version from About Codex]

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After using the Available Reset feature, Codex CLI and
Codex Desktop continue to experience persistent connection
and authentication failures on Windows.

Codex CLI error:

Reconnecting... 5/5

Stream disconnected before completion:
websocket closed by server before response.completed

Codex Desktop error:

unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
Incorrect API key provided.

Endpoint:
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

Environment:
- Codex CLI: 0.157.0
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Authentication: Sign in with ChatGPT
- Platform: Windows
- WinHTTP proxy: Direct access (no proxy server)

Troubleshooting performed:

1. Used the Available Reset feature.
2. Logged out and logged back into ChatGPT successfully.
3. Verified authentication using "codex login status".
   Result: Logged in using ChatGPT.
4. Verified that the account still has available Codex usage.
5. Verified TCP connectivity to OpenAI endpoints on port 443.
6. Confirmed no WinHTTP proxy is configured.
7. Checked PowerShell environment variables.
   No OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY detected.
8. Removed the temporary custom model provider configuration.
   Codex starts normally, but the connection errors persist.

Expected behavior:

Codex CLI and Desktop should successfully authenticate,
establish a connection, and complete requests without
repeated WebSocket disconnections or HTTP 401 errors.

Actual behavior:

Codex CLI repeatedly reconnects and fails before
receiving response.completed.

Codex Desktop returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized despite
a successful ChatGPT login.

The issue persists after using Available Reset
and re-authenticating.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to Codex using a ChatGPT Plus account.
2. Use the "Available Reset" feature in Codex.
3. Open Codex Desktop on Windows.
4. Open an existing conversation or create a new conversation.
5. Send a simple prompt:

   ```
   Hello, respond with OK.
   ```

6. Codex Desktop returns:

   ```
   unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
   Incorrect API key provided.
   ```

7. Open PowerShell and verify Codex authentication:

   ```powershell
   codex login status
   ```

   Output:

   ```
   Logged in using ChatGPT
   ```

8. Start Codex CLI:

   ```powershell
   codex
   ```

9. Send the same prompt:

   ```
   Hello, respond with OK.
   ```

10. Codex CLI repeatedly attempts to reconnect and eventually fails:

    ```
    Reconnecting... 5/5

    Stream disconnected before completion:
    websocket closed by server before response.completed
    ```

### Additional Context

- Codex CLI version: 0.157.0
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Operating system: Windows
- Authentication: Sign in with ChatGPT
- Available usage: Approximately 99% (5-hour limit) and 100% (weekly limit) when checked.
- WinHTTP proxy: Direct access (no proxy server).
- TCP connectivity to OpenAI endpoints on port 443: Successful.
- No OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY environment variables detected in PowerShell.

The issue persists after logging out and logging back into ChatGPT.

### Expected Result

Codex CLI and Codex Desktop should successfully authenticate
and complete requests after using Available Reset.

### Actual Result

Codex Desktop returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

Codex CLI repeatedly disconnects before receiving
the response.completed event.

Both applications are unable to complete requests reliably.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
### Summary

Codex CLI on Windows reports **Logged in using ChatGPT**, stores a normal OAuth/JWT access token, and has no configured API key, but requests to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` fail with:

```
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
```

The `sk-svcac...` credential shown in the server error is **not** the access token stored in `~/.codex/auth.json`.

### Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26200, x64)
- PowerShell 7.6.6
- npm-managed Codex CLI via fnm / Node v24.18.0
- Tested Codex CLI versions:
  - 0.156.0
  - 0.156.1
  - 0.157.0
- Model: `gpt-6-sol`
- Provider: `openai`

### Auth state

`codex login status`:

```
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

`codex doctor` reports:

```
auth storage mode        File
auth file                C:\Users\<user>\.codex\auth.json
stored auth mode         chatgpt
stored API key           false
stored ChatGPT tokens    true
```

There are no `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` environment variables set.

The stored access token metadata is:

```
AccessTokenPresent  : True
AccessTokenLength   : 1872
AccessTokenPrefix   : eyJhbGciOiJS
RefreshTokenPresent : True
RefreshTokenLength  : 211
```

So the stored access token is a normal JWT-style OAuth token, not an `sk-svcac...` key.

### Reproduction

1. Kill all Codex CLI/helper processes.
2. Cleanly install Codex 0.157.0:
   ```powershell
   npm install -g @openai/codex@0.157.0
   ```
3. Run:
   ```powershell
   codex logout
   codex login
   ```
4. Browser OAuth completes successfully.
5. Confirm:
   ```powershell
   codex login status
   ```
   → `Logged in using ChatGPT`
6. Run:
   ```powershell
   codex exec "Reply with exactly: AUTH OK"
   ```

### Actual result

Codex retries WebSocket transport, falls back to HTTPS, then fails:

```
ERROR: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA.
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
request id: 862e97bf-ac5b-4bb4-ad43-321b29c1c9fb
cf-ray: a40dc0070957d71d-BNE
```

The same failure reproduces on 0.156.0, 0.156.1, and 0.157.0.

### Connectivity / doctor

`codex doctor` reports:

```
websocket connected (HTTP 101 Switching Protocols)
auth mode chatgpt
endpoint wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/<redacted>
ChatGPT inference URL https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/<redacted> reachable (HTTP 405)
```

So DNS/reachability/WebSocket handshake are working.

### Additional cleanup already attempted

- Fresh `codex logout` / `codex login`
- Killed all Codex CLI/helper processes
- Reinstalled CLI cleanly after killing processes
- Verified no custom `model_provider` or `base_url`
- Verified no `OPENAI_*` / `CODEX_*` environment variables
- Verified `auth.json` contains ChatGPT OAuth tokens and no stored API key
- Tested 0.156.0, 0.156.1, 0.157.0

### Expected result

A ChatGPT-authenticated session should use the stored OAuth credential (or correctly derived ChatGPT service credential) and complete the request successfully instead of returning `invalid_api_key`.

### Suspected failure point

Something in the Codex/ChatGPT auth path appears to be replacing or translating the valid stored OAuth token into an invalid `sk-svcac...` credential before the request reaches `/backend-api/codex/responses`.

Happy to provide a redacted `codex doctor --json` report or additional request IDs if useful.

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop and Codex CLI both return `401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...` when using ChatGPT subscription auth, even though the stored ChatGPT access token is valid when tested directly against the Codex backend.

This started immediately after updating the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app and switching to Astra. I want to stay on current builds / Astra rather than downgrade.

## Environment

- macOS on Apple Silicon
- Codex CLI tested on:
  - 0.157.0
  - 0.155.0
- `codex login status`: `Logged in using ChatGPT`
- No `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` environment variables are set
- Desktop app was also rolled back to an older build, but the same 401 persisted
- `~/.codex/config.toml` has no custom `model_provider` or `base_url`
- Forcing `model_provider="openai"` still returns 401

## Auth troubleshooting already performed

1. Normal ChatGPT login
2. `codex logout` followed by fresh login
3. Device-code login via `codex login --device-auth`
4. Verified `~/.codex/auth.json`:
   - `auth_mode = chatgpt`
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY = None`
   - token dictionary present
   - fresh `last_refresh`
5. Confirmed no environment overrides with:
   ```
   env | grep -E 'OPENAI|CODEX'
   ```
   (no output)

## Key diagnostic

Using the access token from `~/.codex/auth.json` directly against:

`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

returns **HTTP 400**, not 401:

```
{"detail":"The 'None' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}
```

This indicates the ChatGPT bearer token is accepted by the backend.

However, Codex CLI and Desktop using the same auth state return:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

This strongly suggests the client is not attaching/using the ChatGPT bearer token correctly and is instead sending or surfacing an API-key-style credential.

## Expected behavior

Codex should use the ChatGPT subscription session/token and successfully call the Codex backend, including when using Astra.

## Actual behavior

CLI and Desktop both fail with 401 despite valid ChatGPT auth and a bearer token that is accepted when used directly.

## Notes

I can provide a fresh request ID / cf-ray from a failing request if useful.

items.body:
## Description

Codex CLI 0.157.0 on macOS Apple Silicon consistently fails with:

`401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...`

even though Codex is configured to authenticate using ChatGPT, no API key is stored, and `codex doctor --json` reports the ChatGPT authentication configuration as valid.

The issue affects both the interactive Codex CLI and `codex exec`.

Logging out and logging back in with ChatGPT does not resolve the issue.

Updating Codex CLI from 0.154.0 to 0.157.0 also did not resolve it.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.157.0`
- Platform: macOS 26.6.2
- Architecture: Apple Silicon / macOS aarch64
- Model: `gpt-5.6-sol`
- Provider: `openai`
- Authentication: ChatGPT
- Installation: standalone Unix installer
- Current executable: `$HOME/.local/bin/codex`

## Authentication status

`codex login status`:

```text
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

Relevant output from `codex doctor --json`:

```text
auth.credentials:
- status: ok
- stored API key: false
- stored ChatGPT tokens: true
- stored agent identity: false
- stored auth mode: chatgpt
```

The environment does **not** contain `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_*` variables.

There are no project `.env` files.

There is no custom `model_provider`, `base_url`, `wire_api`, or `preferred_auth_method` configured in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

## Network diagnostics

`codex doctor --json` reports:

```text
network.provider_reachability:
- status: ok
- ChatGPT inference URL reachable
- reachability mode: ChatGPT auth

network.websocket_reachability:
- status: ok
- Responses WebSocket handshake succeeded
- handshake result: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols
- auth mode: chatgpt
- model provider: openai
- wire API: responses
```

No proxy environment variables are configured.

System proxy is direct.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate with ChatGPT:

   ```bash
   codex logout
   codex login
   ```

2. Verify authentication:

   ```bash
   codex login status
   ```

   Result:

   ```text
   Logged in using ChatGPT
   ```

3. Run Codex interactively and send a simple prompt:

   ```text
   TEST OK
   ```

4. Codex returns:

   ```text
   401 Unauthorized
   Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...
   ```

5. The same issue can be reproduced using:

   ```bash
   codex exec "Odpowiedz tylko: TEST OK"
   ```

## `codex exec` result

Command:

```bash
codex exec "Odpowiedz tylko: TEST OK"
```

Output begins normally:

```text
OpenAI Codex v0.157.0
workdir: $HOME/Documents/service-copilot
model: gpt-5.6-sol
provider: openai
approval: on-request
sandbox: workspace-write
reasoning effort: high
```

Then Codex repeatedly reconnects:

```text
ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 3/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 4/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
```

It then falls back from WebSockets:

```text
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport.
stream disconnected before completion:
websocket closed by server before response.completed
```

After another reconnect sequence, HTTPS fails with:

```text
ERROR: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...[redacted]
```

URL:

```text
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

Request ID:

```text
22a590f1-abff-4062-9ee3-a58544004e8d
```

Cloudflare Ray:

```text
a40db6051b31daab-MUC
```

## Expected behavior

Codex should use the stored ChatGPT authentication tokens and successfully process the request through the ChatGPT Codex backend.

## Actual behavior

Codex reports that ChatGPT authentication is configured correctly and that no API key is stored.

However, when an actual inference request is made, the backend rejects a credential beginning with:

```text
sk-svcac...
```

as an invalid API key.

This appears inconsistent with the local authentication state reported by Codex:

```text
stored API key: false
stored ChatGPT tokens: true
stored auth mode: chatgpt
```

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Verified `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not set
- Verified no `CODEX_*` environment overrides are present
- Verified no project `.env` files exist
- Verified no custom provider/base URL configuration exists
- Ran `codex logout`
- Ran `codex login` using ChatGPT
- Verified `codex login status`
- Updated Codex CLI from 0.154.0 to 0.157.0
- Tested a new Codex session
- Tested interactive Codex
- Tested `codex exec`
- Ran `codex doctor --json`
- Confirmed ChatGPT auth configuration is OK
- Confirmed HTTP provider reachability
- Confirmed WebSocket handshake succeeds with HTTP 101
- Confirmed no proxy is configured

The issue remains fully reproducible.

## Additional observation

The WebSocket connection initially succeeds according to `codex doctor`, but during inference the server closes the stream before `response.completed`.

Codex then falls back to HTTPS, where the request is rejected with the 401 `Incorrect API key` response.

This may indicate that the credential used for the actual inference request differs from, or is handled differently than, the ChatGPT authentication state validated by `codex doctor`.

## Security note

The complete `sk-svcac...` credential has intentionally not been included in this report.

I can provide additional diagnostic output or request IDs if needed.

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?
ChatGPT desktop 26.924.20706 (macOS 27.0), bundled codex; codex-cli 0.157.0.

### What issue are you seeing?
With managed deny-read requirements and **no** `allowed_permission_profiles` / `allowed_sandbox_modes`, the desktop permissions menu shows **Full access** as selectable. Selecting it and sending a message fails:

```
failed to load configuration: `approval_policy = "never"` cannot be used because requirements do not allow `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`; Codex would fall back to read-only permissions with approvals disabled. Choose an `approval_policy` based on what you need, such as `on-request`, or choose an allowed sandbox mode.
```

The runtime behaviour is correct and matches the docs ("When deny-read requirements are present, the local runtime rejects full-access permissions"). The menu is not: per the permission-modes docs, "A mode that isn't allowed appears disabled". It looks like the menu only consults the allowlists and ignores `deny_read`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. `/etc/codex/requirements.toml`:
   ```toml
   [permissions.filesystem]
   deny_read = ["~/.ssh", "~/Library/Keychains", "~/**/.env"]
   ```
2. `~/.codex/config.toml`: `default_permissions = ":workspace"`.
3. Restart the desktop app, open Work on a local project, open the permissions menu → Full access is enabled.
4. Select Full access and send any message → the chat fails to start with the error above.

For comparison: adding `allowed_sandbox_modes = ["read-only", "workspace-write"]` makes the menu show "Full access — Disabled by requirements.toml".

### Expected behavior
Full access is shown as disabled ("Disabled by requirements.toml") whenever managed `deny_read` is present, since the runtime will reject it anyway.

items.body:
### Summary

On Linux, Codex Desktop/CLI reports **Logged in using ChatGPT**, has valid-looking OAuth tokens, but every request to the ChatGPT Codex backend fails with:

```
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac…fvMA
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

A fresh ChatGPT login recreates an `OPENAI_API_KEY` field in `~/.codex/auth.json`, even though `auth_mode` is `chatgpt`. Removing that field manually does not resolve the failure; after a fresh login it is recreated and the same 401 returns.

### Environment

- Linux x86_64 (Arch/Omarchy)
- Package: `openai-codex-desktop`
- Desktop build tested: `26.915.31945-1`
  - Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.9.2`
- Rolled back and reproduced on: `26.915.31029-1`
  - Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.9`
- Auth method: ChatGPT
- `codex login status`: `Logged in using ChatGPT`
- No `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` key/token variables in the shell environment
- No matching variables in `systemctl --user show-environment`

### Reproduction

1. Sign in with ChatGPT:
   ```
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex logout
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex login
   ```
2. Confirm:
   ```
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex login status
   Logged in using ChatGPT
   ```
3. Inspect `~/.codex/auth.json` metadata (values redacted):
   ```
   auth_mode: chatgpt
   OPENAI_API_KEY present: True
   access token present: True
   refresh token present: True
   ```
4. Run:
   ```
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "reply with exactly: auth works"
   ```
5. WebSocket transport retries and falls back to HTTPS.
6. HTTPS request fails with:
   ```
   401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac…fvMA
   url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
   ```

### Additional troubleshooting

- Removed only `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `~/.codex/auth.json`; `auth_mode: chatgpt` and OAuth access/refresh tokens remained present.
- Retesting still produced the same masked `sk-svcac…fvMA` credential and the same 401.
- Performed a full `codex logout` + fresh ChatGPT login.
- Fresh login regenerated `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the failure remained.
- Rolled Desktop back from `26.915.31945-1` / CLI `0.155.0-alpha.9.2` to `26.915.31029-1` / CLI `0.155.0-alpha.9`; failure is identical.
- WebSocket failure appears secondary because HTTPS fallback fails with the same 401.

### Expected behavior

When `auth_mode` is `chatgpt` and `codex login status` reports a valid ChatGPT login, requests to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` should use the ChatGPT OAuth/session credential path and succeed.

### Actual behavior

The client appears to send or derive an `sk-svcac…` API/service key for the ChatGPT backend, which is rejected as an incorrect API key.

### Related issues

This looks related to recent ChatGPT-auth 401 reports such as #39883 and #41975, but this repro is on Linux and specifically shows:
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` being recreated by a fresh ChatGPT login,
- the same masked service-key-shaped credential surviving manual removal of that field,
- identical behavior across two Desktop builds / bundled CLI revisions.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex suddenly stopped working.

Authentication succeeds normally:

- `codex login` completes successfully
- `codex login status` reports: `Logged in using ChatGPT`
- `codex doctor --json` reports:
  - stored API key: false
  - stored ChatGPT tokens: true
  - stored auth mode: chatgpt
  - WebSocket handshake: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols

However, any inference request fails.

Example:
╭────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ >_ OpenAI Codex (v0.157.0)                     │
│                                                │
│ model:     GPT-6-Sol medium   /model to change │
│ directory: /mnt/projects/Projects/webcalendar  │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

hi

ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 3/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 4/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport. stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
ERROR: Reconnecting... 1/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 2/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 3/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 4/5
ERROR: Reconnecting... 5/5
■ unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac*REDACTED*. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys., url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses, cf-ray: REDACTED

This is unexpected because I am logged in using ChatGPT OAuth, not an API key.

The issue reproduces:
- after `codex logout` + `codex login`
- in a fresh session
- with `codex exec "responda apenas OK"`
- on Codex 0.156.1
- after updating to Codex 0.157.0

There are no `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_*` environment variables set.

It was working normally a few hours before this started.

Uploaded thread: 01a0dac7-ff68-70b3-acb3-025fd2bab23d

Suppress console windows for local Windows MCP servers

## What changed

Expose Windows process creation flags on the shared command wrapper and use
`CREATE_NO_WINDOW` when launching local stdio MCP servers, including fallback
launches without Job Object containment. Preserve `CREATE_SUSPENDED` when
assigning the server to a Job Object before execution.

## Testing

Add a Windows regression test covering direct launches and launches through
`cmd.exe`. Verify that the server has no console, initializes successfully,
returns tools, and exits after shutdown.

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop and Codex CLI both began failing suddenly with 401 Unauthorized after working normally all day. Re-authenticating in both clients does not resolve the issue.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.155.1`
- Login status: `Logged in using ChatGPT`
- Remote Linux server for CLI
- ChatGPT desktop app also affected
- User had been actively authenticated and using Codex successfully before the failure began

## Desktop error

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac[REDACTED].
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

The error included a Cloudflare ray ID and request ID, but the credential itself is intentionally redacted here.

## What has been tried

1. Verified CLI version
2. Confirmed `codex login status` reports `Logged in using ChatGPT`
3. Logged out and back in on Codex CLI
4. Logged out and back in on the desktop app
5. Same 401 persists in both environments

## Why this looks server-side/account-routing related

- Both Desktop and CLI started failing at roughly the same time
- Both had been working normally earlier the same day
- Fresh ChatGPT authentication does not resolve the failure
- The failing endpoint is the ChatGPT Codex backend: `/backend-api/codex/responses`

Please investigate whether there is an auth-routing/session issue affecting ChatGPT-authenticated Codex traffic even though the public status page currently shows green.

items.body:
### What happened

Remote compaction fails with a 401. The rejected key is an OpenAI **service-account key** (`sk-svcacct-…`), but that key isn't configured anywhere on the client. The session shows "Compaction interrupted" followed by "Reconnecting 2/…".

```
Error running remote compact task: unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac***…fvMA. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys., url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses, cf-ray: a40d8b075ce54801-SJC, request id: f7192488-dccb-430c-a65f-d5884bb4228c
```

### Why this looks server-side

- The client is logged in with ChatGPT (`auth_mode: chatgpt` in `~/.codex/auth.json`, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` there is null).
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not set in the environment.
- No custom `model_provider` or `env_key` is set in `config.toml`.
- A second user on a different machine and account hit the same error at the same time.

So the `sk-svcacct` key seems to belong to the backend's remote-compaction path, and it's being rejected.

### Environment

- codex-cli 0.157.0
- macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
- Auth: ChatGPT login

### Steps to reproduce

Use a ChatGPT-authenticated Codex session until auto-compaction triggers.

### Expected

Compaction succeeds, or at least doesn't fail with an unrelated service-account key.

### IDs for tracing

- request id: `f7192488-dccb-430c-a65f-d5884bb4228c`
- cf-ray: `a40d8b075ce54801-SJC`

items.title: Windows elevated sandbox recursively grants ACEs on `%USERPROFILE%\AppData` on every setup refresh; user profile ended unusable (regression of #12343; related #31140, #47104)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, the elevated sandbox setup grants read ACEs to the sandbox users on the **whole
`%USERPROFILE%\AppData` tree**, and on a number of other profile paths. It re-applies them on every
setup refresh: 96 refreshes on one day and 42 on another, from the logs.

After about five weeks of this, the interactive profile became unusable:
- explorer crash-looped every ~2 s in `windows.immersiveshell.serviceprovider.dll`, `0x80270233`;
- AppX packages (CBS, CoreAI/ClickToDo, CrossDevice, AAD.BrokerPlugin) failed with `0x80070005` when
  registering or writing HKCU;
- a TEMP profile of the same user worked fine.

Stripping the sandbox ACEs from the profile files, about 1.34M objects carrying SIDs of
`CodexSandboxUsers`/`Offline`/`Online`, did not recover it. The profile had to be recreated.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200, AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395
- codex-cli 0.154.0-alpha.6.2 → 0.155.0 → 0.156.0 (npm)
- Codex App 26.917.x (Microsoft Store). It auto-updated at 22:07 on the day the profile broke; that update
  shipped a new `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe`.
- `~/.codex/config.toml` had `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`

## Evidence: `~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.YYYY-MM-DD.log`

```
granting read ACE to C:\Users\<user>\AppData for sandbox users
granting read ACE to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu for sandbox users
granting read ACE to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCookies for sandbox users   (from 2026-08-18)
granting read ACE to C:\Users\<user>\.claude.json for sandbox users
granting write ACE to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp for sandbox group and capability SID
granting write ACE to D:\GitHub\<repo> for sandbox group and capability SID
applied deny ACE to protect D:\GitHub\<repo>\.git
read-acl-only mode: applying read ACLs      (x91 on 2026-09-14, x33 on 2026-09-18)
setup refresh: processed N write roots (read roots delegated); errors=[]
hide users: failed to hide current user profile dir (C:\Users\Default): SetFileAttributesW failed ... Access is denied.
junction: failed to create C:\Users\Default\.codex\.sandbox\cwd: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

`AppData` contains `Local\Packages`, the AppX per-user data, and `Local\Microsoft\Windows\UsrClass.dat`,
the per-user classes hive. Recursively re-ACLing it while the user is logged on, repeatedly, is the most
likely way the AppX state was damaged. We could not prove the exact final step, because the logs for the
last day were written to throwaway `CODEX_HOME`s (see below).

## How Codex was run

- Interactively through Codex App and CLI.
- Non-interactively as a coding executor:
  `codex exec --approve-for-me -c tools.web_search=false -c tools.image_gen=false --json …`
  - a throwaway `CODEX_HOME` whose `config.toml` sets only `model` and `model_reasoning_effort`, with
    **no `[windows]` section**, so whatever the default is;
  - `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` redirected to a temp directory, while `APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA` still pointed at
    the real profile. We suspect this is where the `AppData` read root comes from.

## Expected

- The sandbox never grants recursive ACEs on the profile root, `AppData`, `AppData\Local`, or
  `AppData\Roaming`. Read access to those should not require rewriting their DACLs.
- Setup refresh is idempotent. It does not re-walk and re-apply ACLs on every command.
- There is a documented cleanup command that removes every ACE and account the sandbox created.
- The default for `[windows] sandbox` when it is unset, including under `exec --approve-for-me`, is
  documented.
- The Codex App `CodexSandboxService` (LocalSystem, auto-start) makes elevated setup possible without a
  UAC prompt. That should be an explicit opt-in.

## Workaround

- `[windows] sandbox = "unelevated"`, both in the user config and in any throwaway `CODEX_HOME`.
- Delete `CodexSandboxOffline`, `CodexSandboxOnline`, and `CodexSandboxUsers`.
- Recreate the profile if it is already broken.

### What happened

In an existing Codex TUI, I switched to the affected session using `/resume`. The session appeared open and showed `Ready`, but the TUI did not process submitted input for many minutes. The original `codex.exe` process (PID 2512) remained alive and was observed using substantial CPU. It later became usable again without an apparent restart.

I tried `codex resume 01a0ca2d-d02e-7ac2-a23f-7b600faf579f` in two other PowerShell tabs. Both showed "This conversation is open in another app." That lock message is expected while the first instance owns the thread; it did not help because the owner was unresponsive. Pressing the displayed `q` exit key in the waiting tabs did not appear to work promptly either.

### Expected behavior

The owning TUI should continue processing input after resuming, or show progress while it is busy. A second TUI waiting for the writer lock should process its documented exit key promptly.

### Local timeline (23 September 2026, Europe/Berlin)

- 10:31:48 — The prior session's turn completed in PID 2512.
- 10:32:22 — PID 2512 entered `thread/resume` for the affected session and acquired its writer lock. Session initialization and MCP startup activity were logged through 10:32:30.
- 10:34:40 — PID 9212 logged `thread-store conflict: thread ... already has an active writer`.
- 10:35:23 — PID 43348 logged the same conflict.
- During the reported stall, the processes remained alive and were observed consuming substantial CPU. Subsequently, the original process became idle and the UI recovered. No corresponding Windows crash event was found.

The affected rollout was 8,233,778 bytes with 2,670 valid JSONL records and two compaction records. Its last event at 10:32:22 was `thread_settings_applied`; it has no new `task_started` event during the stall. The resume also logged 71 `dropping turn-scoped item for unknown turn id` warnings within less than one millisecond. I cannot establish that those warnings caused the later delay.

### Assessment

The later `resume` attempts encountered a real active writer. The unresolved behavior is that the owning CLI/TUI held the session while it stopped processing user input and consumed CPU, then recovered. History preparation or TUI rendering is a possibility, but no thread stack or CPU profile was captured during the stall. The exact hotspot and recovery time remain unknown.

### Reporting limitation

Attempting to use `/feedback` from a separate Codex TUI produced `Failed to upload feedback: feedback/upload failed in TUI`; no feedback ID or successful upload was shown. I do not know whether that failure is related.

Related reports: #34724 (slow resume of a much larger thread), #39823 (active-writer conflicts after session switching), #41174 (feedback upload error). None establishes the cause of this incident.

Sanitized excerpts from the local Codex log database and screenshots can be provided if useful.

items.title: Preserve model and access program pairs during compaction
items.body:
Preserve model and access program pairs during compaction

## Why

Compaction using the previous model can inherit the current turn's access program, producing a model/program pair that the server rejects.

## What changed

- Persist `cyber_access_program` in previous-turn settings and restore it during rollout reconstruction.
- Use the previous turn's access program when compacting with its model, preserving an absent program instead of inheriting the current selection.
- Pass the selected access program into local compaction prompts.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for local and remote compaction after model switches, including resume, fork, rollback, and compaction checkpoints. Verify fallback and subsequent sampling use the current model/program pair, and API-key sessions do not inherit access-program authorization.
