items.title: VS Code: closing the owning Codex tab leaves a Goal running invisibly and consuming usage

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt 26.917.62051`

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 5x (US$100/month tier)

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 6.8.0-139-generic x86_64 x86_64`

### What issue are you seeing?

An active Codex Goal continued executing after I closed its VS Code conversation tab. I returned hours later and discovered that the session had remained active even though no tab exposed its progress or a Stop control.

This is a major lifecycle and usage-control defect. Closing the only visible owner of an interactive run creates the reasonable expectation that the run has stopped, or at minimum that Codex will ask whether it should continue in the background. Instead, work can continue silently, consume paid usage/rate-limit capacity, and conflict with later work while the user has no visible control surface.

The problem is broader than a missing notification:

- no persistent global indicator showed that the detached run was still active;
- no global Stop control was available once its tab was gone;
- the user could not inspect what it was doing or how much usage it was consuming;
- closing or restarting VS Code did not provide a clear orphaned-run reconciliation flow;
- later session ownership/resume failures made it difficult to recover control.

In the same failure period, the extension also displayed these errors:

```text
This is open in another app
Close it there to continue here.
```

and:

```text
Error submitting message
App-server queued follow-up no longer exists
```

Those messages may be related ownership-state symptoms rather than the same root cause. They are included because the invisible run and stale ownership behavior occurred in the same workflow.

This fails minimum lifecycle and billing-control expectations for an agentic tool. A paid, tool-capable process must never become both active and invisible merely because its owning tab or window disappeared.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed path:

1. Open a Codex conversation in the VS Code extension.
2. Start a long-running Goal that can automatically continue across turns.
3. Close the conversation tab while the Goal is still active.
4. Leave VS Code or close/restart it.
5. Return later.
6. Observe that the Goal/session continued running without its original tab, without a persistent global active-run indicator, and without an accessible Stop control.
7. Attempt to reopen/resume the session and encounter stale ownership or queued-follow-up errors in some cases.

I have one confirmed occurrence. I have not yet reduced it to a deterministic minimal reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex needs an explicit and enforceable ownership contract:

1. Closing the last tab/window that owns an interactive run should stop or pause it by default.
2. Continuing after UI detachment should require explicit user opt-in to a background run.
3. Every active background run should appear in a persistent global activity surface, with thread name, elapsed time, model, usage, current state, and a working Stop control.
4. On VS Code shutdown/restart, Codex should deterministically reattach, pause, or cancel every orphaned run and clearly report the result.
5. The extension should retain an auditable lifecycle record: started, detached, continued, paused/stopped, completed, and usage consumed while detached.
6. If the frontend loses contact with the app-server or active turn, the backend should enter a bounded grace period and then pause/cancel unless explicit background authorization exists.

If silent continuation is intended behavior for Goals, requirements 2 through 6 are still mandatory. Invisible paid execution without a reliable global cancel surface is unacceptable.

### Additional information

The official Goals documentation describes a Goal as a user-controlled completion contract, states that interruptions pause it, and says lifecycle authority remains controlled by the user or system. The observed behavior left the user without that control after the owning UI disappeared:

https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex

Potentially related reports:

- #39911 — VS Code panel disappears while work continues in the background
- #20131 — VS Code cannot reopen sessions that the CLI can resume
- #24287 — active work becomes invisible and Stop fails in Codex Desktop
- #35463 — silent multi-agent execution can drain subscription quota

No internal task content, repository identifiers, session IDs, or private logs are included here. Sanitized diagnostics can be supplied through a private channel if maintainers specify what to collect.

items.title: Preserve late result metadata for truncated code-mode calls
items.body:
Preserve late result metadata for truncated code-mode calls

## Why

When a nested code-mode call's recorded arguments were truncated and attached to an output before its result arrived, the recorder could no longer attach the result metadata to that call.

## What changed

Retain validated call bindings so late result metadata updates the original output across retries and subsequent waits. Keep truncated arguments and incomplete call inventories intact, and apply existing metadata budgets.

Invalidate late metadata bindings when duplicate IDs, reused cells, conflicting outputs, or changed call inventories make attribution ambiguous. Clear stale pending calls when a cell ID is reused, and avoid counting duplicate pending IDs against capacity more than once.

## Testing

Add recorder regression tests for late metadata across retries, compaction, waits, and cell closure, plus ambiguous bindings and budget limits. Add a code-mode integration test that delays a tool result until its truncated call has been recorded and verifies metadata remains attached to the original output across later waits.

items.title: [macOS] 26.924.20706 update triggers Gatekeeper “malware” removal for OpenAI-signed codex during CLI repackaging

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Desktop bundle version `26.924.20706`, build `11431` (`com.openai.codex`, installed as `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`).

Bundled CLI layout under:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/
```

The package layout matches the new CLI packaging reported in #48214.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS on Apple Silicon.

### What issue are you seeing?

Immediately after applying the in-app update to `26.924.20706 (11431)`, macOS displayed a system warning that the Codex update had been identified as malware and was moved to Trash.

The update was initiated from the existing official OpenAI desktop app's built-in update UI. No third-party download site or manually downloaded installer was involved.

The installed app remained present and usable after the warning.

A review of macOS Unified Logging shows that, during the update, Gatekeeper evaluated OpenAI-signed Codex components and then classified one standalone `codex` code object as blocked code and attempted to move it to Trash.

The relevant object was identified by macOS as:

```text
team: 2DC432GLL2
id: codex
bundle_id: NOT_A_BUNDLE
```

Immediately before the block, `syspolicyd` logged repeated:

```text
Error checking with notarization daemon: 3
```

The block occurred at approximately `2026-09-25 13:39:10` local time.

Relevant log sequence:

```text
2026-09-25 13:39:10.663 ... GK evaluateScanResult: 2, ... (team: 2DC432GLL2), (id: codex), (bundle_id: NOT_A_BUNDLE) ...
2026-09-25 13:39:10.663 ... Attempting to move malware to trash: ... (team: 2DC432GLL2), (id: codex), (bundle_id: NOT_A_BUNDLE)
2026-09-25 13:39:10.663 ... moveItemToTrashWithReply
...
2026-09-25 13:39:10.781 ... Sent CloudTelemetry event: MalwareDiscoveredLite
2026-09-25 13:39:10.844 ... Sent CloudTelemetry event: MalwareDiscovered2
2026-09-25 13:39:10.844 ... Evaluating blocked code: ... (team: 2DC432GLL2), (id: codex), (bundle_id: NOT_A_BUNDLE)
...
2026-09-25 13:39:10.875 ... Attempting to move malware to trash
2026-09-25 13:39:10.885 ... Successfully moved malware to trash
```

A few minutes later, `syspolicyd` again evaluated blocked code with the same path token and `id: codex`.

### Current installed state

The main desktop app currently passes code-signature and Gatekeeper checks:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app: valid on disk
/Applications/ChatGPT.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement
/Applications/ChatGPT.app: accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
origin=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)

Identifier=com.openai.codex
Authority=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)
Authority=Developer ID Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
TeamIdentifier=2DC432GLL2
```

The updated bundle contains:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex
```

The `bin/codex` file is only a 328-byte POSIX shell wrapper:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
entry="$0"
while [ -L "$entry" ]; do
  parent=$(CDPATH= cd -P -- "$(dirname -- "$entry")" && pwd)
  entry=$(readlink "$entry")
  case "$entry" in /*) ;; *) entry="$parent/$entry" ;; esac
done
bin_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -P -- "$(dirname -- "$entry")" && pwd)
exec "$bin_dir/../CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex" "$@"
```

The real Codex Mach-O executable is:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex
```

It currently verifies successfully:

```text
Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64
valid on disk
satisfies its Designated Requirement

Identifier=codex
Authority=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)
Authority=Developer ID Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
Timestamp=Sep 23, 2026 at 7:58:36 AM
TeamIdentifier=2DC432GLL2

accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
origin=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)
```

SHA-256 of the currently installed real Codex executable:

```text
c3e30211bd454da70ceb4d9cbc2e05fe6466812ab05c311c3bbff6addeb14202
```

Filesystem timestamp:

```text
Sep 25 13:38:56 2026
```

This is only about 14 seconds before the Gatekeeper block at `13:39:10`.

The outer `CodexCLI.app` also currently passes Gatekeeper:

```text
valid on disk
satisfies its Designated Requirement
accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
origin=Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)
```

No file matching `*codex*` remained in the user's Trash when checked afterward.

### Reproduction / observed sequence

1. Start from a legitimate installed ChatGPT/Codex desktop app.
2. Allow the app to download the offered in-app update.
3. Click the normal in-app update control.
4. Observe the update downloading/installing.
5. Immediately receive a macOS warning that Codex/update code was malware and had been moved to Trash.
6. Inspect Unified Logs around the update timestamp.
7. Observe repeated notarization daemon errors followed by Gatekeeper classifying an OpenAI-signed `codex` object as blocked and moving it to Trash.
8. After installation, verify that the resulting app bundle, `CodexCLI.app`, and real `codex` Mach-O all pass signature and Gatekeeper assessment.

### Expected behavior

A legitimate in-app update should not cause macOS Gatekeeper/XProtect to classify an OpenAI-signed Codex component as malware or move it to Trash.

All executable components in the update and any staging copies used during installation should be signed/notarized in a way that macOS accepts consistently throughout the update process.

### Additional context

This may be related to the CLI repackaging introduced in `26.924.20706`. #48214 reports that this exact build changed the bundled CLI layout from the prior `Resources/codex` path to the new `Resources/codex-cli/...` layout and caused CLI-path regressions on multiple Apple Silicon Macs.

This report is distinct: the issue here is a Gatekeeper/XProtect malware-removal event during the update, not a dangling PATH symlink.

The currently installed code is accepted as notarized OpenAI software, so the available evidence is consistent with a transient Gatekeeper/notarization/staging failure or false positive during installation. This report does **not** establish that the blocked object contained malicious code.

If useful, I can provide a narrower excerpt of the Unified Log around `13:39:05–13:39:11`.

items.title: [Linux][Desktop] Codex corrupts shared fontconfig cache (cache-12 symlinked as cache-9/10/11), causing KDE Plasma and Qt apps to SIGSEGV

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
## Summary

Launching Codex Desktop on Kubuntu 24.04 reproducibly rewrites my user
fontconfig cache in `~/.cache/fontconfig` using cache format 12 and creates
compatibility symlinks from older cache filenames (`cache-9`, `cache-10`,
`cache-11`) to the `cache-12` files.

After this happens, KDE Plasma and other Qt/KDE applications begin crashing
with SIGSEGV in fontconfig. `plasmashell` crashes shortly after startup,
leaving a black desktop with only the mouse cursor visible.

Removing the corrupted cache and regenerating it with the system
`/usr/bin/fc-cache` immediately restores the desktop.

Launching Codex Desktop again reproduces the corruption and the crashes.

This is therefore reproducible A/B on the same machine.

## Environment

- OS: Kubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Architecture: x86_64
- Desktop: KDE Plasma
- Codex / ChatGPT Desktop package: `chatgpt` amd64
- Current package version: 26.924.20706
- Previous package version: 26.917.71314
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4080 SUPER
- Package installed from the official OpenAI Linux repository

Additional environment information can be provided if needed.

## Reproduction

1. Make sure Codex Desktop is not running.

2. Remove/move the existing user fontconfig cache and regenerate it with
   the system fontconfig:

   ```bash
   mv ~/.cache/fontconfig ~/.cache/fontconfig.backup
   mkdir -p ~/.cache/fontconfig
   /usr/bin/fc-cache -f

3. Verify that there are no cache-format-12 files or compatibility symlinks:
   find ~/.cache/fontconfig -maxdepth 1 \
     \( -name '*.cache-12' -o -type l \) \
     -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM:%TS %y %f -> %l\n' | sort
   
   Output is empty.
4. At this point KDE Plasma and Qt applications work normally.
5. Launch Codex Desktop.
6. Immediately after launching Codex, the following files appear in
   ~/.cache/fontconfig:
   4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-12
   4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-9
      -> 4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-12
   4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-10
      -> 4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-12
   4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-11
      -> 4c599c202bc5c08e2d34565a40eac3b2-le64.cache-12
   
   The same pattern is created for multiple font directories.
7. KDE/Qt applications then begin crashing. plasmashell reproducibly
   terminates with:
   Signal: Segmentation fault (11)
   Executable: plasmashell
   
   The desktop becomes black, although KWin/the X session remains alive
   and a Konsole window can still be opened by keyboard shortcut.
8. Stop Codex, delete/move the fontconfig cache again, and regenerate it:
   mv ~/.cache/fontconfig ~/.cache/fontconfig.bad
   mkdir -p ~/.cache/fontconfig
   /usr/bin/fc-cache -f
   
   Plasma and other Qt/KDE applications immediately become stable again.
9. Launching Codex Desktop once more reproduces steps 6-7.
Actual behavior
Codex appears to use a newer bundled fontconfig/cache implementation and
writes format-12 cache files into the host user's shared
~/.cache/fontconfig.
It additionally creates older-format filenames as symlinks to the
format-12 files.
The host system fontconfig subsequently appears to consume those files as
its own cache format, resulting in invalid memory access / SIGSEGV in
applications using the system fontconfig library.
The impact is system-wide: it is not limited to Codex itself. Plasma,
Kate, KRunner and other KDE/Qt applications are affected.
Expected behavior
Codex and its bundled runtime must not write an incompatible fontconfig
cache into the host user's shared fontconfig cache directory.
If the bundled runtime requires a newer fontconfig cache format, it should
use an isolated cache location, for example a Codex-specific
XDG_CACHE_HOME / fontconfig cache directory.
Launching Codex must not be capable of making unrelated host desktop
applications crash.
Recovery
The machine can be recovered without reinstalling KDE or NVIDIA drivers by:
1. terminating Codex;
2. moving/removing ~/.cache/fontconfig;
3. rebuilding the cache specifically with /usr/bin/fc-cache -f.
After this, Plasma is stable until Codex Desktop is launched again.
Notes
This was reproduced multiple times.
The timestamps of the cache-12 files and the cache-9/10/11 -> cache-12
symlinks correspond to the Codex launch.
Before launching Codex after a clean cache rebuild, the files are absent.
Immediately after launching Codex, they appear and KDE starts crashing.
There are already Codex issues discussing bundled fontconfig runtimes and
the need for isolated XDG_CACHE_HOME, but I could not find an existing
report describing this host-cache corruption and system-wide KDE crash.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Windows Store/MSIX package:

`OpenAI.Codex 26.924.1866.0`

Package full name:

`OpenAI.Codex_26.924.1866.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

Immediately after updating Codex Desktop to `26.924.1866.0`, the main window opens as a gray screen with an infinite loading spinner and never becomes usable.

The interesting part is that the Codex backend is clearly still alive:

- tasks started remotely through SSH / phone continue to run;
- the Codex Pet/avatar overlay in the same Windows app still shows live progress from those tasks;
- `thread/list` and `thread/read` requests return successfully with `errorCode=null`;
- the main renderer then repeatedly logs `Conversation state not found`;
- incoming remote-task events are initially logged as `Received turn/started for unknown conversation`, after which Desktop emits `Rebinding placeholder latest turn to incoming event` and continues receiving reasoning progress;
- this happens for both the primary renderer and the `avatarOverlay` renderer.

So the app-server/backend path appears responsive, while the Desktop conversation-state / hydration layer does not recover and the primary UI remains stuck on the loader.

The problem started immediately after the update. I have not reset or deleted `~/.codex` because the backend sessions are still working correctly.

### Relevant sanitized log excerpts

Desktop logs are under:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\...`

Representative startup/session sequence:

```text
info  [AppServerConnection] response_routed ... method=thread/read ... errorCode=null
error [electron-message-handler] Conversation state not found conversationId=<redacted> rendererWindowAppearance=primary

info  [AppServerConnection] response_routed ... method=thread/list ... errorCode=null
```

The same pattern repeats across multiple existing conversations:

```text
info  [AppServerConnection] response_routed ... method=thread/read ... errorCode=null
error [electron-message-handler] Conversation state not found ... rendererWindowAppearance=primary
```

When a task is started remotely over SSH:

```text
error [electron-message-handler] Received turn/started for unknown conversation ... rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay
error [electron-message-handler] Received turn/started for unknown conversation ... rendererWindowAppearance=primary

info  [AppServerConnection] response_routed ... method=thread/read ... errorCode=null

error [electron-message-handler] Conversation state not found ... rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay
error [electron-message-handler] Conversation state not found ... rendererWindowAppearance=primary
```

A few seconds later the event stream partially recovers:

```text
warning [electron-message-handler] Rebinding placeholder latest turn to incoming event ... rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay
warning [electron-message-handler] Rebinding placeholder latest turn to incoming event ... rendererWindowAppearance=primary

info [electron-message-handler] Reasoning summary item completed ... rendererWindowAppearance=primary
info [electron-message-handler] Reasoning summary item completed ... rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay
```

This matches the visible behavior: the Pet continues to show task progress while the main window remains stuck on the gray loading screen.

No recent Crashpad reports were present in the checked MSIX Crashpad reports directory.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have Codex Desktop working normally on Windows.
2. Update to `26.924.1866.0`.
3. Launch Codex Desktop.
4. Observe the gray window with an infinite loading spinner.
5. Start or continue a Codex task from another client/remote SSH session.
6. Observe that the Windows Pet/avatar overlay still shows live task progress while the primary Desktop UI never finishes loading.
7. Check Desktop logs: successful `thread/read` / `thread/list` responses are followed by repeated `Conversation state not found` and `unknown conversation` renderer errors.

### Expected behavior

The Desktop renderer should hydrate/register conversation state after successful `thread/list` / `thread/read` responses and finish loading the main UI.

A remote task event should not remain unknown to the primary renderer after the backend has successfully returned the thread state.

### Additional information

This looks like a Desktop renderer/conversation-state regression rather than a broken Codex backend:

- remote tasks continue executing;
- the Pet overlay continues receiving progress;
- app-server responses are successful;
- the primary UI alone remains stuck.

Potentially related issues with similar log fingerprints include #32737, #47054, #47985, and the recent startup/loading regression #48148, but this report is specifically for Windows Desktop `26.924.1866.0` and reproduces immediately after updating to that build.

items.title: Windows desktop app: uncaught "write EPIPE" in IpcRouter on every update restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What happened

Almost every time the Codex desktop app restarts to install an update on Windows, an error dialog pops up:

> **A JavaScript error occurred in the main process**
> Uncaught Exception: Error: write EPIPE

```
Error: write EPIPE
    at afterWriteDispatched (node:internal/stream_base_commons:159:15)
    at writeGeneric (node:internal/stream_base_commons:150:3)
    at Socket._writeGeneric (node:net:1171:11)
    at Socket._write (node:net:1183:8)
    at doWrite (node:internal/streams/writable:596:12)
    at clearBuffer (node:internal/streams/writable:781:7)
    at onwrite (node:internal/streams/writable:651:7)
    at WritableState.onwrite [as callback] (node:internal/streams/writable:350:26)
    at WriteWrap.onWriteComplete [as oncomplete] (node:internal/stream_base_commons:105:10)
```

No data is lost: threads are saved before the crash and the update installs. But the dialog shows up every time.

### Frequency

I checked my desktop logs. Since 2026-09-12 this has happened on 8 update restarts, and it has never happened at any other time.

### Relevant log excerpt (crash at 2026-09-25 20:56 UTC)

```
20:56:06.011Z info update_resume_state_saved threadCount=0
20:56:08.605Z info update_resume_state_saved threadCount=0
20:56:09.175Z info [AppServerConnection] Stopping app-server transport connectionId=1 transport=stdio
20:56:09.177Z info [AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.state_changed cause=stop_process ... previous=connected next=disconnected
20:56:09.210Z warning [electron-message-handler] chatgpt_pubsub_transport_closed ...
20:56:09.646Z warning [IpcRouter] Socket error errorCode=EPIPE errorMessage="write EPIPE"   (x4)
20:56:09.648Z warning [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=ipc-connection-reset   (x5)
20:56:09.899Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE removed browser session window windowId=1
```

`IpcRouter` logs 4 socket errors, and then one more write fails without being handled (note the `clearBuffer` path in the stack trace), which crashes the main process. My guess is that the error listener is removed, or the socket is destroyed, after the first error while buffered writes are still pending. No external clients were connected: no `codex` CLI, no IDE extension, no other Node processes.

### Environment

- Codex desktop app (MSIX) `OpenAI.Codex_26.924.1866.0_x64` (installed version after the update)
- Crashing session: buildNumber `10954`, commit `da68906ecca788ec45aa4d449cb841473e5ed2bf`, bundled codex `0.155.0-alpha.16.4`
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 (x64)

### Also noticed (possibly unrelated)

While the app is running, this warning is logged every 30 seconds:

```
[install-primary-runtime] primary_runtime_update_poll_failed errorMessage="Windows primary runtime framework requires a configured MSIX release with a bundle version."
```

### Expected

The app should shut down cleanly for the update, without an uncaught-exception dialog. EPIPE on IPC sockets during shutdown should be handled or ignored.

items.title: [macOS app] Update to 26.924.20706 leaves bundled Codex CLI symlinks dangling

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop bundle version `26.924.20706`, build `11431` (`com.openai.codex`, installed as `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`).

Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. The failure occurs during local executable discovery, before a model request.

### What platform is your computer?

Reproduced on three Apple Silicon Macs, all running macOS 26.6.2 (25G83).

```text
Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm
```

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating the desktop app on all three Macs, project entries showed red status indicators with this tooltip:

> Codex CLI is not installed on this machine

Each machine had an existing PATH entry that was a symlink to the app's bundled CLI:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/codex
  -> /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex
```

The target no longer exists in the updated bundle. Although `/opt/homebrew/bin` is on PATH, executable discovery fails; `shutil.which("codex")` returned `None` on all three machines.

The CLI is still present and executable at the new packaged entry point:

```text
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex
```

The package manifest `codex-cli/codex-package.json` reports:

```json
{
  "layoutVersion": 1,
  "version": "0.158.0-alpha.2",
  "target": "aarch64-apple-darwin",
  "variant": "codex",
  "entrypoint": "bin/codex",
  "resourcesDir": "codex-resources",
  "pathDir": "codex-path"
}
```

**Scope:** this report concerns existing links to the app-bundled CLI, not a verified failure of separately installed npm/Homebrew CLI packages. The location under `/opt/homebrew/bin` does not establish that Homebrew created the link; the original creator of these links has not been established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have a working `codex` command on PATH linked to `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex`.
2. Update the desktop app to `26.924.20706` (build `11431`).
3. Inspect the link: its previous target is absent.
4. Observe CLI discovery failure and the project status indicating that the CLI is not installed.
5. Invoke the new bundle entry point directly:

```sh
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex --version
```

This succeeds with `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2`.

### What is the expected behavior?

If the previous bundled entry point is supported, retain a compatibility launcher or migrate app-managed command links when changing the package layout.

If direct links to bundled CLI paths are unsupported, please document a stable supported launcher and provide an actionable diagnosis for a dangling CLI link, rather than only reporting that the CLI is not installed.

### Additional information

**Verified workaround:** on all three machines, replaced the existing dangling symlink with a link to the package's declared `bin/codex` entry point. After that, both ordinary and login zsh shells successfully resolved the command and returned the expected version:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/codex
codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2
```

The repair did not reinstall the CLI, modify the app bundle, or change project data. This verifies executable discovery and version execution; the sidebar's refreshed badge state has not yet been independently verified.

The current [desktop troubleshooting documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting) still references `/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex` as a retained compatibility entry point. That compatibility bundle was not present on these installations either.

Related but distinct: #32495 describes an earlier app-name migration and helper lookup failure. This report concerns the subsequent move from `Resources/codex` to the new `Resources/codex-cli/` package layout, leaving the command link unable to start the CLI at all.

No session transcripts, credentials, private project names, or network details are attached.

items.title: Isolate executable fixture copies in CLI tests on Linux
items.body:
Isolate executable fixture copies in CLI tests on Linux

## Why

Sibling tests can spawn children while an executable fixture is open for
writing, allowing inherited writable descriptors to cause `ETXTBSY` when
launching the fixture.

## What changed

Add a shared `copy_executable` helper for the daemon, doctor path safety, and
exec-server tests. On Linux, run `/bin/cp` in a separate process and wait for
it to exit before launching the fixture, then restore the source permissions
to account for restrictive umasks. Keep `std::fs::copy` on other platforms.

items.title: Preserve queued output for observers during code-mode termination
items.body:
Preserve queued output for observers during code-mode termination

## Why

Yield signals and queued runtime events can detach an observer during termination, before the remaining output has been drained.

## What changed

Track the active yield signal separately from the observer so termination can disable yielding while keeping the observer attached. Ignore `Started`, `Pending`, and `YieldRequested` events during termination, allowing queued output to reach the observer in `CellEvent::Terminated`.

## Testing

Extend the termination regression test with an immediate yield timeout, a canceled yield signal, and queued start, yield, output, and completion events. Assert that both the termination caller and the initial observer receive the queued output in the terminated event.

items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

Windows package **26.917.9434.0**; application release **26.917.71314** as reported in the local logs. Investigated on **25 September 2026**.

## What subscription do you have?

Not specified in this public report. The isolated failure is in local sidebar/menu identity lookup and does not depend on subscription state.

## What platform is your computer?

`Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64`

## What issue are you seeing?

The context menu for some existing local Codex chats omits the entire **Project** submenu, including moving the chat to another project and removing it from its current project. The rest of the context menu opens normally. The affected chats have valid saved project assignments.

This concerns the context menu of **one local chat in the sidebar**, not the conversation-header menu, a selection of multiple chats, or a cloud ChatGPT conversation.

The user confirmed that **File > Quit**, followed by relaunching Codex, restores the missing submenu for the affected chats. Closing the last window with **X** normally hides it in the system tray in this build and does not restart the renderer.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

### UI conditions observed

1. In the Windows desktop app, create a local chat through the foreground creation flow and send its initial prompt.
2. Allow creation to finish and the permanent conversation ID to become available.
3. Right-click the chat's sidebar row. Affected rows retain a temporary identity for sidebar stability and lack **Project** in the resulting menu.
4. Fully quit using **File > Quit**, relaunch, and right-click that existing chat again. **Project**, including the move/remove actions, returns.

The original affected renderer state was not captured directly. Steps 1–3 describe the lifecycle demonstrated by source inspection and isolated execution; the complete UI sequence has not been independently repeated on a clean installation. Full quit restoring the reported affected chats was confirmed by the user.

### Deterministic isolated reproduction

The installed menu builder was executed with synthetic fixtures. The failing precondition is that a sidebar row has a temporary key but its underlying task points to the permanent conversation ID. This semantic example uses invented identifiers:

```js
const conversationId = "example-conversation";
const row = {
  task: {
    key: "local:client-new-thread:example-client",
    conversationId,
  },
};
const rows = [row];

// Equivalent identity comparison in the affected menu builder:
const wrong = rows.find(
  item => item.task.key === `local:${conversationId}`,
); // undefined -> early empty action list -> no Project submenu

// Resolve the underlying local conversation identity instead:
const correct = rows.find(
  item => item.task.conversationId === conversationId,
); // row
```

The example abstracts the bundle's existing task-accessor functions; it is not a reproduction of their complete object schema. Nine isolated scenarios passed during the investigation, including pending creation, preserved identity after creation cleanup, permanent IDs, and a fresh renderer retaining saved aliases but clearing volatile bindings. The original code fails for preserved temporary IDs and succeeds after the canonical-ID correction.

## What is the expected behavior?

A completed local chat should expose its applicable **Project** actions whether its sidebar row uses its permanent conversation ID or a preserved temporary client ID. Navigation and account-session history should not require a full application restart to recover those actions.

## Additional information

### Root-cause evidence and confidence

There is a **confirmed defect in isolated execution of this installed build**, and it is the **high-confidence explanation** for the reported symptom:

1. Foreground creation begins with a temporary client ID.
2. Binding to the permanent conversation ID can preserve that client ID for sidebar stability.
3. Creation cleanup removes the pending task while leaving the binding intact.
4. Sidebar construction therefore uses the preserved temporary ID for the row key.
5. The Project-menu builder searches for a key generated from the permanent conversation ID instead. The failed lookup returns an empty action list before project assignment is consulted.

In this build, the relevant menu builder is minified as `uUs`. It compares a sidebar task's key with `Hw(conversationId)`, while sidebar construction can use `Hw(sjn(get, conversationId))`. The mismatch explains why both move and remove disappear together while unrelated menu items remain.

Local saved-state and session-log evidence support this lifecycle for the affected chats; no private logs or real chat identifiers are included here. The in-memory renderer was not inspected before restart, so this report does not claim a direct memory capture of the original failure. It also does not establish which release first introduced the defect. Account switching was considered, but was not established as the trigger.

### Proposed correction — unofficial, not an OpenAI release

Resolve the sidebar row through the existing canonical conversation-ID accessor, as the move/drop handler already does. When falling back to project-group membership, use the **matched row's actual key**:

```js
const row = allSidebarItems.find(
  item => canonicalConversationId(item.task) === conversationId,
);
if (!row) return [];

const sourceGroup = projectGroups.find(
  group => group.threadKeys.includes(row.task.key),
);
```

The existing explicit project-assignment lookup retains its precedence over the membership fallback. This report proposes a narrowly scoped correction, not a rewrite of sidebar identity handling. Regression coverage includes permanent and temporary row keys, explicit assignments and membership fallback, move/remove callback IDs, unsupported/nonlocal rows, and idempotent patch detection.

The concrete two-fragment diff tested against the original JavaScript asset is:

```diff
-a.find(e=>e.task.key===s)
+a.find(e=>tT(e.task)===t)
-l==null?e.threadKeys.includes(s):e.projectId===l.projectId
+l==null?e.threadKeys.includes(c.task.key):e.projectId===l.projectId
```

Here `t` is the requested canonical conversation ID, `c` is the matched row, `tT` is the existing canonical-ID accessor, and `s` is the key synthesized from the permanent ID. These are surgical replacements inside the reviewed menu builder, not global replacements for arbitrary bundles.

A locally prepared patch is **unofficial**. This report does not claim that OpenAI has accepted it, shipped it, or released a permanent fix.

### Completed validation

- **29/29 tests passed, with no failures or skips**: 17 menu/transformation tests and 12 archive tests. Menu coverage includes permanent and aliased row keys, explicit assignment precedence, membership fallback, canonical move/remove callback payloads, nonlocal/unknown/pending rows, host restrictions, pinned/projectless source containers, idempotency, unsupported hashes, changed signatures, partial fixes, and invalid UTF-8.
- A lookup-only correction still fails to offer Remove when membership falls back to a group containing the temporary key. The second correction is needed for that case.
- The actual installed archive was read and a repaired archive was staged separately. The target JavaScript's integrity metadata was updated, every unrelated packed byte was verified unchanged, and the original archive was rehashed and remained unchanged. Repeating staging produced the same archive hash. Archive tests also cover invalid integrity metadata, malformed/overlapping offsets, ambiguous/unpacked targets, existing destinations, input/output protection, failure cleanup, and source-path replacement detection.
- The signed Microsoft Store application was **not modified**. A separate copied app containing this repair passed an isolated-profile startup check: its primary renderer started and its local backend connected. Existing environment overrides select the copied bundled CLI and disable the copied app's Store updater. The bundled and original registered CLI versions both report `0.155.0-alpha.16.4`. Live-profile menu behavior is still awaiting verification; no supported in-place Store installation is claimed.

The original reviewed JavaScript SHA-256 is `34a60939a5f44634a65c956b7904d63236178e6d45a049717358fc163ecffe88`; the derived repaired JavaScript SHA-256 is `8b9824de98b195be6ed8cb2a533a3fc585fc775a135e083023fd09fa2af883bd`. These identify the JavaScript asset, not the full archive. The shareable tools contain the small transformation and synthetic tests, not the proprietary bundle or private app state.

### Handling later releases

The local transformation accepts only the exact reviewed defective bundle and recognizes the exact repaired bundle as a no-op. Unknown hashes or changed signatures stop without modifying the application; they are not evidence that a vendor fix exists. A later version must be inspected and tested afresh. If its current menu implementation passes these cases, retire the local correction for that version. Otherwise, review and validate a new minimal correction before adding that exact version's hashes. Never copy an older patched archive over a newer release. Any future deployment/restore procedure must bind its backup and integrity checks to the exact package being changed.

### Workaround

Use **File > Quit**, then relaunch. Allow active work to finish or stop it intentionally before quitting. Merely closing the last window with **X** normally leaves the same renderer alive through tray behavior. New chats can trigger the defect again later in the session.

### Related reports and public fix status

Checked on **25 September 2026**:

- [#35826](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35826) reports a missing move action for **cloud chats** on Windows in a July build. This report isolates a local-task sidebar identity failure.
- [#35473](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35473) reports missing project actions on macOS; full quitting reportedly did not resolve that case.
- A [community analysis in #28141](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28141#issuecomment-4953033965) describes a similar temporary/permanent ID mismatch in terminal handling. It is not confirmation of this Project-menu diagnosis.
- No exact public report, OpenAI-published RCA, or released fix was found in the searched tracker and [official changelog](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog). This does not establish the status of internal OpenAI tickets.

This report follows the [Codex App Bug template](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/1-codex-app.yml). It intentionally excludes account identifiers, real chat titles/IDs, local filesystem paths, raw logs, and the application's bundled source.


## Downloadable fix, tests, and future-release procedure

[Download codex-project-menu-fix-v1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32669586/codex-project-menu-fix-v1.zip)

ZIP SHA-256: `412f69473edd648a82f48bd558ad5e222864b12acf02ca3bfa008e9f0a265104`.

The attachment contains the minimal diff, guarded JavaScript/ASAR patcher, 29 regression tests, exact version/hash manifest, a separate-copy builder and launcher, validation results, and instructions for reviewing later releases. It contains no application binaries, original bundled source, credentials, private logs, or conversation data.

The current Store package is retained unchanged. A separate patched copy passed an isolated startup check with the existing `CODEX_CLI_PATH` override pointing to its hash-verified bundled runtime and `CODEX_SPARKLE_ENABLED=false` for the copied app. The primary renderer started and the local backend connected, with no bootstrap/package-identity error. This establishes isolated startup, not exhaustive validation of package-dependent integrations or live-profile menu behavior.

The launcher prevents concurrent use of the same live profile and refuses this older copy once the registered Store version changes. Future unknown releases must be reviewed/tested individually; the scripts deliberately do not blindly reapply the patch or replace newer archives with older ones.

items.title: [Windows Desktop 26.917] 5/5 browser-session end events followed by 90–150s app hang

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

items.body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26200, x64
- Microsoft Store package `OpenAI.Codex` 26.917.8451.0 (`ChatGPT.exe`)
- Bundled Codex runtime 0.155.0-alpha.16.3
- Git 2.55.0.windows.3
- A newer desktop package, 26.917.9434.0, is available but has not yet been installed. The user reports intermittent freezes have persisted through earlier updates.

## Symptom

The entire desktop window intermittently becomes unresponsive for about 90–150 seconds, then recovers without a restart. This happens while tasks progress, around task completion, and sometimes while no task appears active. Windows Error Reporting recorded `AppHangTransient` for `ChatGPT.exe` at 2026-09-25 22:27:42 Australia/Sydney, and an earlier event at 2026-09-24 22:10:02.

## 90-minute monitored capture

A local monitor sampled the main window's Windows `Responding` flag, process private memory, and Git process count every five seconds from 2026-09-25 21:30:31 to 23:00:28 AEST (UTC+10). It recorded five continuous unresponsive episodes:

| Unresponsive samples, AEST | Main-process private memory, approximate | Git processes in unresponsive samples |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 21:34:28–21:36:24 | 371 MB baseline → 1,120 MB peak → baseline | 0 |
| 21:40:25–21:41:51 | 365 MB → 1,128 MB → baseline | 0 |
| 22:13:54–22:15:55 | 370 MB → 1,125 MB → baseline | 0 |
| 22:25:39–22:27:40 | 365 MB → 871 MB → baseline | 0 |
| 22:35:33–22:37:59 | 371 MB → 854 MB → baseline | 0 |

In that same monitoring interval, the desktop log recorded **exactly five** `IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity` events. Each preceded one of the five hangs by **1.6–5.1 seconds**. No additional unresponsive samples appeared through the end of monitoring. This is a strong timing association, but the available data do not prove the blocking call or root cause.

Selected desktop log lines (UTC; conversation IDs removed):

```text
2026-09-25T11:34:23.611Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity disposeAfterSessionActivity=false windowId=1
2026-09-25T11:40:22.529Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity disposeAfterSessionActivity=false windowId=1
2026-09-25T12:13:53.161Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity disposeAfterSessionActivity=true windowId=1
2026-09-25T12:25:34.287Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity disposeAfterSessionActivity=true windowId=1
2026-09-25T12:35:31.203Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity disposeAfterSessionActivity=false windowId=1
2026-09-25T12:38:01.260Z info [sampler-manager] main_thread_jank_snapshot mainThreadJankCountSinceLastSnapshot=2 processRole=browser_main snapshotReason=heartbeat windowAttention=visible_unfocused
```

The main desktop log was largely quiet during each hang and resumed with `main_thread_jank_snapshot` around recovery. The primary renderer also logged repeated `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications`, including outside hang intervals, so that message is not treated as causal evidence.

## Checks and attempted isolation

- Hiding the floating pet, restarting the app, switching to a smaller task, and upgrading Git did not stop the freezes.
- Temporarily disabling Windows notifications did not stop three subsequent hangs; the notification setting was restored.
- Direct `git status` outside the desktop app took about 72 ms. Git worker timeouts do appear elsewhere in the logs, but no Git process was present during any sampled hang.
- `codex doctor` reported healthy local databases and a consistent desktop installation.
- User configuration and agent routing were preserved. The bundled browser plugin has not been disabled for this test.

Related but distinct reports: #22655 describes turn-complete/browser-route hangs and exits; #25094 describes short freezes around browser-sidebar startup. This capture points specifically to browser-use **session-end** events followed by two-minute recoverable hangs.

## Question for maintainers

Is this a known desktop/browser-session cleanup defect in 26.917, and is there a verified fix or safe workaround that preserves the user's browser and agent configuration? If a hang-time stack or trace is needed, please advise the preferred private diagnostic collection and submission path. Raw desktop logs, session transcripts, local paths, and task content are intentionally omitted from this public report because they may contain private information.

## Private feedback reference

The user also submitted diagnostics through Codex `/feedback`. Feedback/session reference: `01a0cdf5-05bb-7a83-8a74-3403580e12a6`. Please correlate that private submission with this issue; the raw diagnostics are not posted publicly.

items.title: Keep archived threads with empty previews visible in listings
items.body:
Keep archived threads with empty previews visible in listings

## Why

Archived threads without previews were filtered out of thread listings, even though they had valid session metadata.

## What changed

- Include archived threads with empty previews in both SQLite and rollout-file listings.
- Add archive-specific indexes for creation, update, and recency ordering so these listings can use indexed pagination.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for paginated archive listings with and without SQLite, archive query plans that avoid temporary sorting, and metadata reads that preserve source and file timestamps for empty archived threads.

items.title: Honor execution environment proxy requirements
items.body:
Honor execution environment proxy requirements

## Why

An execution environment's enabled proxy configuration was reduced to traffic restrictions, leaving restricted commands offline without a controller proxy or an approved network grant.

## What changed

Carry `NetworkProxyConfig.enabled` into `EnvironmentNetworkPolicy.requires_proxy` and honor it when activating managed networking. This lets environment owners require filtered proxy access while direct network access remains restricted. Policies without an explicit proxy requirement retain the existing activation behavior.

## Testing

Extend remote command coverage to check allowed and denied proxy requests without a controller proxy, and verify that direct network access remains blocked.

items.title: CLI: make `daemon_auto_start` opt-in — a persistent, self-updating background daemon shouldn't be the default

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI — 0.157.0, installed via `npm install -g @openai/codex`, Linux (WSL2)

### What feature would you like to see?

Please make `daemon_auto_start` **opt-in (default `false`) for the CLI**, or at least ask once before turning it on.

Since 0.157.0, just opening an interactive `codex` session:

1. **Starts a persistent background daemon** (`codex app-server --managed-daemon`). It runs in its own session with no TTY and keeps running after every Codex window is closed (reparented to PID 1) until `codex app-server daemon stop` or a reboot.
2. **Copies the whole platform package** (~374 MB: `codex`, `codex-code-mode-host`, bundled `bwrap`/`zsh`/`rg`) into `~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/<version>/` — byte-identical to what npm had just installed — and runs the daemon from that copy. From then on the backend's version is decoupled from the CLI version I installed with my package manager.
3. **Starts a detached updater** (`codex app-server daemon pid-update-loop`) that checks for updates 5 minutes after start and then hourly, downloads new releases and restarts the backend (which can kill active turns, see #40969).
4. **Pins the environment of whichever session happened to start it.** I launch Codex through a wrapper that sets `HTTPS_PROXY` per invocation; the daemon keeps the first session's proxy variables and its outbound connections go through that proxy, whatever later sessions are launched with. #42457 and #37537 (daemon cwd / terminal instead of the session's) look like the same root cause.

For a CLI, the least surprising default is that the backend lives and dies with the window, runs the binary I installed, and doesn't update itself in the background. A shared, self-updating daemon makes sense for Remote Control / the desktop app, so it would be fine to enable it there, or when the user explicitly runs `codex app-server daemon start` / `bootstrap`.

If it stays on by default, please at least:
- exit an auto-started daemon when its last client disconnects;
- not copy/self-update when the CLI was installed by a package manager (npm/brew/pacman) — run the installed binary instead (#41188, #46468, #48050).

### Additional information

**Bug found while turning it off:** `codex app-server daemon stop` stops the app-server but leaves the `pid-update-loop` updater running (still alive 70 s later, had to kill it manually).

Workaround I'm using:

```sh
codex features disable daemon_auto_start
codex app-server daemon stop
pkill -f 'app-server daemon pid-update-loop'   # not stopped by `daemon stop`
rm -rf ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon
```

With the flag off, a new TUI session no longer spawns a daemon.

Related: #40969, #41188, #46468, #48050, #42457, #37537

items.body:
## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.157.0` (latest according to `codex doctor`)
- Codex Desktop installed: `26.917.9434.0` (not running during the diagnostic; update `26.924.1866.0` was available)
- Model: `gpt-5.6-sol`
- Authentication: ChatGPT subscription (exact tier not known)
- OS: Windows 11 CoreSingleLanguage, `10.0.26200`, x64, language `es-MX`
- Terminal metadata detected by Codex: VS Code `1.137.0`
- Shell: PowerShell `7.6.6`
- Install method: npm, Windows x86_64
- Git: Git for Windows at `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`

## What issue are you seeing?

While Codex is generating a response or executing normal agent/tool work, visible console/terminal windows intermittently flash open and close. This is not triggered by manually opening the integrated terminal.

At the same time, links rendered in Codex responses can become unusable: I cannot select the link text, copy it, or activate the link reliably. This makes it difficult to open or copy GitHub links and other references from the response.

The console symptom is periodic rather than a single popup. During a 20-second read-only process capture while Codex was active, **9 new `conhost.exe` processes** were observed, roughly one every 2.1–2.2 seconds:

```text
16:55:55.895 conhost.exe
16:55:58.012 conhost.exe
16:56:00.294 conhost.exe
16:56:02.450 conhost.exe
16:56:04.642 conhost.exe
16:56:06.838 conhost.exe
16:56:09.075 conhost.exe
16:56:11.193 conhost.exe
16:56:13.427 conhost.exe
```

The windows are short-lived, so the command line and parent PID could not be captured with ordinary polling. A WMI process-start trace was attempted, but Windows denied access. No manual commands were launched during the capture.

This looks related to #24910, but that report concerns an older Codex Desktop build and specifically identifies `git.exe`. In this case the active environment is Codex CLI/VS Code, the CLI is current, and the process that can be consistently observed is repeated `conhost.exe` creation. The unselectable response links may also be related to the UI symptom mentioned in #47910.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex on Windows from the VS Code/Codex environment.
2. Open a repository and ask Codex to perform a task that generates a response and uses local tools.
3. Leave Codex working for at least 20-30 seconds.
4. Observe short-lived console windows flashing open and closing repeatedly.
5. Try to select, copy, or activate a Markdown link in the generated response.
6. Observe that the link may not be selectable/copyable/clickable while this behavior is occurring.

The issue is intermittent from the user's perspective, but process sampling reproduced the `conhost.exe` creation at a regular interval during an active response.

## What is the expected behavior?

- Background commands and helper processes should run without creating visible console windows.
- Codex should not spawn a new console host every few seconds during normal response generation.
- Response links should remain selectable, copyable, and clickable while Codex is working.
- Focus should not be stolen from the editor or chat UI by short-lived console windows.

## Codex doctor report

`codex doctor --json` completed successfully with overall status `warning`.

Relevant results (personal paths redacted):

```json
{
  "overallStatus": "warning",
  "codexVersion": "0.157.0",
  "app_server.status": "ok: background server is running (0.157.0)",
  "auth.credentials": "ok: ChatGPT auth is configured",
  "config.load": "ok: model gpt-5.6-sol",
  "desktop.app.version": "installed: 26.917.9434.0; not running during diagnostic",
  "git.environment": "ok: Git for Windows detected",
  "installation": "ok: npm installation is consistent",
  "network.provider_reachability": "ok",
  "network.websocket_reachability": "ok: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols",
  "runtime.provenance": "npm on windows-x86_64",
  "terminal.env": "VS Code 1.137.0",
  "updates.status": "CLI current at 0.157.0; Desktop update 26.924.1866.0 available"
}
```

The unrelated doctor warnings were: repository not on a Windows Dev Drive, optional MCP configuration, Microsoft Defender exclusions not verified, and one rollout/state inventory mismatch. There were no install, authentication, connectivity, Git detection, or database-integrity failures.

## Additional information

- The problem has occurred repeatedly, not only once.
- Restarting the response/task does not make the flashing windows predictable.
- The exact executable inside the flashing console is difficult to read because the window closes almost immediately.
- A screen recording or a higher-privilege ETW/WMI process trace can be provided if maintainers need the precise parent process and command line.

- medium
- high
- xhigh
- max
- ultra
The backend can run Astra successfully.
Using codex app-server --stdio, I sent a direct turn/start to the same thread with:
{
  "threadId": "01a0d9e7-ce57-7523-b171-b86f6856e34d",
  "model": "gpt-6-astra",
  "effort": "high",
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Reply with exactly: ASTRA TEST"
    }
  ]
}

The turn completed successfully and returned:
ASTRA TEST

After this direct call, the thread persisted as:
model = gpt-6-astra
reasoning_effort = high

This proves:
- account access is fine
- model catalog is fine
- ARM64 backend is fine
- app-server is fine
- Astra/high works on the same thread
- the issue is in Codex Desktop’s model-selection / turn-start path
- 
Likely fault
Desktop appears to send or derive gpt-5.5 / xhigh during the first turn/start, overriding:
- the configured default model
- the persisted composer model
- the user’s explicit model selection
The Desktop UI then reflects that effective thread setting and appears to “snap back”.

Repro
1. Set:model = "gpt-6-astra"
   model_reasoning_effort = "high"
2. Open Codex Desktop.
3. Start a new chat.
4. Select GPT-6 Astra / High.
5. Selection immediately reverts to GPT-5.5 Extra High.
6. Inspect the new thread in state_5.sqlite or its rollout JSONL.
7. New thread is persisted as gpt-5.5 / xhigh.
8. Send a direct turn/start through app-server with gpt-6-astra / high.
9. It succeeds.
Additional note
A clean reinstall of the ARM64 Codex Desktop build did not change the behaviour.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Steps to reproduce:
1. On Windows 11 ARM64, install/open Codex Desktop.
2. Set C:\Users\<user>\.codex\config.toml to:model = "gpt-6-astra"
   model_reasoning_effort = "high"
3. Open Codex Desktop and create a new chat.
4. Open the model picker.
5. Select GPT-6 Astra with High reasoning.
6. Observe that the UI immediately snaps back to GPT-5.5 Extra High.
7. Send a message in the new chat, for example hello.
8. Inspect the resulting thread in state_5.sqlite or the rollout JSONL.
9. Observe that the thread/first turn is persisted as:model = gpt-5.5
   reasoning_effort = xhigh
10. As a control, send a direct turn/start to the same thread through codex app-server --stdio with:model = gpt-6-astra
    effort = high
11. Observe that the turn completes successfully on Astra/high, confirming the backend supports the requested model and the issue is specific to Codex Desktop’s model-selection/turn-start behaviour.

### What is the expected behavior?

I can change the model using the gui - CLI works fine but the gui is not working.

### Additional information

I have tried using wingetui/windows store and msix offline installs/uninstalls/reinstalls. clearing the application folders the lot. I do not have the same problem on macos or windows x64, but my dell xps 13 snapdragon elite x1 has this problem suddenly.

items.title: Bound agent message board SSE frames before parsing
items.body:
Bound agent message board SSE frames before parsing

## Why

Checking notification data size after SSE parsing leaves oversized fields and unterminated frames free to accumulate in the parser. Malformed UTF-8 can also be retained indefinitely by the decoder.

## What changed

Enforce `MAX_BODY` on incoming frame bytes before SSE parsing and reject malformed UTF-8 incrementally. Reset the byte count at blank lines, supporting LF, CR, and CRLF across chunks, so the limit applies per frame rather than per connection. Stop reading the source stream after an error.

## Testing

Extend the remote board contract test to cover oversized readiness fields, unterminated fields, and multiline data frames. Verify that a long sequence of heartbeat frames with all three line endings still permits notification delivery.
